Square footage of customer-accessible selling floor space, excluding back-of-house, storage, and office areas. Used for sales per square foot calculations, planogram (POG) planning, and merchandising density analysis.

Total building square footage of the store location, including selling floor, back-of-house, storage, and office space. Used for productivity metrics (sales per square foot), lease accounting, and facility management.

Self-referencing foreign key to the parent region in the geographic hierarchy (e.g., a sub-region rolls up to a macro-region). Null for top-level regions.
Total geographic area of the region expressed in square kilometres. Used for store density analysis, market penetration calculations, and territory planning.
Köppen-Geiger climate classification zone for the region. Influences seasonal merchandise planning, HVAC standards for stores, and cold-chain logistics requirements.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the primary country this region belongs to (e.g., 'GBR', 'USA', 'DEU'). Used for regulatory, tax, and currency alignment.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the primary trading currency used in this region (e.g., 'GBP', 'USD', 'EUR'). Drives pricing, P&L reporting, and financial consolidation.

Primary data privacy regulatory framework applicable to customer data collected in this region (e.g., GDPR for EU, CCPA for California, PDPA for Thailand). Drives consent management and data retention policies.
Indicates whether the e-commerce platform is active and accepting orders for delivery or collection within this region. Drives digital marketing spend allocation and last-mile logistics planning.
Date on which this region definition ceased to be operationally effective. Null for currently active records. Supports SCD-2 history and GDPR audit requirements.
Date from which this region definition became operationally effective. Supports SCD-2 history tracking and enables point-in-time analysis of regional boundaries and assignments.

Region identifier as used in external partner systems, government statistical classifications (e.g., NUTS code in Europe, FIPS code in the USA), or third-party data providers. Enables cross-system reconciliation.
Indicates whether stores in this region operate under a franchise model rather than direct corporate ownership. Affects P&L consolidation, compliance obligations, and operational reporting scope.

Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita for the region expressed in USD, sourced from national statistics or IMF data. Used as a proxy for consumer purchasing power in assortment and pricing strategy.
The calendar year to which the GDP per capita figure refers, enabling users to assess data currency.

Numeric depth of this region within the geographic hierarchy. Level 1 is the top (e.g., global zone), increasing integers represent finer granularity (e.g., country, macro-region, sub-region, district).
Materialised slash-delimited path of region codes from root to this node (e.g., 'GLOBAL/EMEA/UK/NORTH'). Enables efficient subtree queries without recursive CTEs.
First line of the street address for the region's administrative headquarters office. Used for official correspondence, regulatory filings, and field operations coordination.
City in which the region's administrative headquarters is located. Used for correspondence, regulatory filings, and geographic reporting.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the country in which the region's administrative headquarters is located. May differ from the region's operational country in cross-border management structures.
Postal or ZIP code of the region's administrative headquarters. Used for correspondence, tax jurisdiction mapping, and logistics routing.
SCD-2 indicator that is True for the currently active version of the region record and False for superseded historical versions. Simplifies current-state queries without date-range filtering.
IETF BCP 47 language tag representing the primary language used in this region for store communications, signage, and customer-facing content (e.g., 'en-GB', 'fr-FR', 'de-DE').
Decimal latitude of the geographic centroid of the region in WGS-84 coordinate system. Used for mapping, proximity analysis, and logistics optimisation.
Decimal longitude of the geographic centroid of the region in WGS-84 coordinate system. Used for mapping, proximity analysis, and logistics optimisation.
Assessment of the retail market development stage within the region. Drives investment strategy, promotional intensity, and format mix decisions (e.g., emerging markets favour discount formats).
Free-text field for operational notes, boundary change explanations, or special instructions relevant to this region. Intended for internal use by the store operations and data governance teams.

Indicates whether stores in this region are enabled for omnichannel fulfilment capabilities such as click-and-collect (BOPIS), ship-from-store (SFS), and same-day delivery. True means at least one omnichannel service is live.
Estimated total resident population within the region boundary. Sourced from national census or third-party demographic data. Used for market sizing, store count planning, and catchment analysis.
The calendar year to which the population figure refers, enabling users to assess data currency and apply appropriate growth adjustments.

Short, externally-known alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the region across operational systems (e.g., 'NE', 'APAC-SOUTH'). Used in reporting, store master data, and cross-system integration.

Full name of the senior retail operations manager accountable for this region. Used for escalation routing, performance review, and organisational reporting. Classified confidential as it identifies an internal employee in a named role.
Corporate email address of the region manager. Used for automated alerts, escalation workflows, and operational communications. Classified as confidential PII.
Full human-readable name of the region as used in business reporting and store operations (e.g., 'North-East', 'Pacific Rim'). Displayed in dashboards, planograms, and territory management tools.

Current lifecycle status of the region record. 'active' means the region is in use for store assignment and reporting; 'inactive' means it has been decommissioned; 'pending' means it is being set up; 'archived' means it is retained for historical reference only.

Categorical classification of the region's primary business purpose. 'operational' covers day-to-day store management; 'sales' covers revenue territory; 'franchise' covers franchisee groupings; 'distribution' covers supply-chain zones; 'compliance' covers regulatory jurisdictions.

Identifier for the regulatory or compliance zone governing retail operations in this region (e.g., EU Single Market, US Federal, APAC Free Trade Zone). Determines applicable labour, food safety, and consumer protection regulations.
Abbreviated display name for the region used in space-constrained UI elements, POS terminal screens, and printed reports (e.g., 'NE Region', 'SW').

Retail shrinkage rate for the region expressed as a percentage of net sales, encompassing theft, administrative error, and supplier fraud. Used for loss-prevention benchmarking and security resource allocation.

Code identifying the upstream operational system from which this region record was sourced (e.g., the retail merchandising system, the store master data system). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

Same-Store Sales (SSS) index for the region, representing the ratio of current-period comparable store sales to the prior-period baseline. A value above 1.0 indicates positive comp sales growth. Used for regional performance benchmarking.
The fiscal period (e.g., 'FY2023-Q2') used as the baseline for the SSS index calculation. Ensures consistent interpretation of the SSS index across reporting cycles.

Number of active retail locations (hypermarkets, department stores, discount outlets, dark stores, MFCs) currently assigned to this region. Maintained as a denormalised reference figure; authoritative count is derived from the store master.
Planned number of stores to be operating within this region as per the current strategic expansion plan. Used for gap analysis and capital expenditure planning.
Official tax authority jurisdiction code for the region (e.g., state FIPS code in the USA, HMRC region code in the UK). Used for tax filing, audit, and compliance reporting.
Strategic importance tier assigned to the region, used to prioritise capital investment, promotional spend, and field support resources. Tier 1 represents highest-priority markets.
IANA timezone identifier for the region's primary operating timezone (e.g., 'Europe/London', 'America/New_York'). Used for scheduling, trading-hour calculations, and timestamp normalisation.

Timestamp of the most recent modification to this region record in the data platform. Used for incremental load detection, audit trail, and change data capture (CDC) processing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Percentage of the region's population living in urban areas. Influences store format selection (hypermarket vs convenience), omnichannel investment, and last-mile delivery feasibility.
Standard Value Added Tax (VAT) or equivalent sales tax rate applicable in this region, expressed as a percentage. Used for price display, financial reporting, and tax remittance calculations.

description: Identifies the specific Distribution Center (DC) or network of DCs to which this SLA applies. Null indicates the SLA applies to all DCs. Used in Manhattan Associates WMS for DC-level performance tracking.
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS; NRF Distribution Standards

description: For EDI compliance SLAs, specifies the EDI transaction set(s) covered (e.g., '850 Purchase Order', '856 Advance Ship Notice', '810 Invoice'). Null for non-EDI SLA types. Aligns with GS1 EDI standards.
reference: GS1 EDI Standards; NRF EDI Compliance Framework

description: Calendar date on which this SLA definition ceases to be binding. Nullable for open-ended agreements. When populated, triggers SLA expiry workflow in Blue Yonder Demand Planning and SAP S/4HANA.

Calendar date on which this SLA definition becomes contractually binding and enforceable between the retailer and the supplier or 3PL partner. Aligns with purchase order or logistics contract activation.

Performance level at which an SLA breach triggers formal escalation to senior management or executive review, beyond standard penalty processing. Typically set below minimum_threshold_value for critical SLAs.
reference: ISO 9001 Corrective Action; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: Number of calendar days after an SLA breach is detected before penalty assessment is initiated. Allows counterparty time to remediate without immediate financial consequence. Zero indicates no grace period.
reference: NRF Vendor Compliance Standards; ISO 9001 Corrective Action

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this SLA definition record in the lakehouse silver layer. Updated on any field change including status transitions, threshold amendments, or penalty structure updates. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 27001 Audit Trail; GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity

description: For Lead Time SLAs, defines the business event that stops the lead time clock. DC Receipt is standard for supplier SLAs; Store Receipt applies to DSD (Direct Store Delivery); Customer Delivery applies to last-mile SLAs.
reference: NRF Supply Chain Standards; Manhattan Associates WMS; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: For Lead Time SLAs, defines the business event that starts the lead time clock. Purchase Order Issued is the standard start; Order Confirmed starts from supplier acknowledgement; Pick Released starts from warehouse pick; Ship Confirmed starts from carrier pickup.
reference: NRF Supply Chain Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM; GS1 EDI 856

description: How often SLA performance is measured and evaluated against the target threshold. Per-shipment applies to individual delivery SLAs; Weekly/Monthly apply to aggregate fill rate and EDI compliance SLAs.
reference: NRF Supply Chain KPI Framework; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

description: Rolling number of calendar days over which SLA performance is aggregated for evaluation. For example, a 30-day rolling window for monthly fill rate measurement. Works in conjunction with measurement_frequency.
reference: NRF Supply Chain KPI Framework; ISO 9001

description: The floor performance level below which penalty clauses are automatically triggered. Distinct from target_threshold_value which is the aspirational goal. For example, target fill rate may be 98% while minimum acceptable is 95%.
reference: NRF Supply Chain Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Calendar date of the next formal SLA review meeting with the counterparty. Populated based on review_cycle and last review completion. Used to trigger review preparation workflows.
reference: ISO 9001 Management Review; NRF Supplier Management Standards

description: Free-text field for additional context, special conditions, exceptions, or negotiation history relevant to this SLA definition. Not used for structured data. Supports procurement team documentation needs.

The internal business unit or department responsible for managing and enforcing this SLA, e.g., 'Supply Chain Operations', 'Procurement', 'DC Management', 'E-Commerce Fulfillment'. Used for accountability and escalation routing.
reference: NRF Organizational Standards; SAP S/4HANA Organizational Management

description: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO cost center code for the business unit responsible for this SLA. Used for financial allocation of penalty charges and SLA management costs.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; FASB Cost Accounting Standards

description: Maximum financial penalty that can be assessed in a single measurement period, regardless of the degree of SLA breach. Expressed in the contract currency. Protects counterparty from unlimited liability. Confidential contract term.
reference: FASB ASC 606; NRF Vendor Compliance Standards; FTC Consumer Protection

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for penalty amounts defined in this SLA (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Ensures correct financial processing in SAP S/4HANA FI/CO for multi-currency supplier contracts.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FASB ASC 606; SAP S/4HANA FI

description: The rate applied to calculate the financial penalty when SLA performance falls below the minimum threshold. Expressed as a percentage of invoice value for chargeback SLAs or as a fixed rate per unit for volume-based penalties. Confidential contract term.
reference: NRF Vendor Compliance Standards; FASB ASC 606; FTC Pricing Transparency

description: The mechanism by which penalties are applied when SLA thresholds are breached. Chargeback deducts from supplier invoice; Credit Memo issues a financial credit; Service Credit applies to 3PL contract credits; None indicates no financial penalty.
reference: NRF Vendor Compliance Standards; FASB ASC 606; SAP S/4HANA FI

description: The merchandise category or department to which this SLA applies, e.g., 'Grocery', 'Apparel', 'Electronics', 'Household Goods'. Null indicates the SLA applies across all categories for the counterparty. Aligns with the retail merchandising system Merchandising System category hierarchy.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Merchandise Standards

description: Frequency at which this SLA definition is formally reviewed and potentially renegotiated with the counterparty. Drives calendar scheduling for supplier business reviews and contract renewal workflows.
reference: NRF Supplier Management Standards; ISO 9001 Management Review

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this SLA definition, used in EDI communications, vendor contracts, and SAP S/4HANA MM module contract references.
reference: GS1 EDI Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM Contract Management

description: Human-readable name describing the SLA commitment, e.g., 'Supplier Fill Rate SLA Q1 2025' or 'DC On-Time Delivery SLA'. Used in reporting dashboards and contract documentation.

Current lifecycle state of the SLA definition. Draft indicates under review; Active indicates currently enforced; Suspended indicates temporarily paused; Expired indicates past effective period; Terminated indicates cancelled before expiry.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; FASB ASC 606 Contract Lifecycle

description: Categorical classification of the SLA commitment. Fill Rate measures order completion percentage; Lead Time measures supplier delivery duration; On-Time Delivery measures punctuality; EDI Compliance measures electronic data interchange adherence; Order Accuracy measures shipment correctness; Return Processing measures RMA turnaround. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fill_rate|lead_time|on_time_delivery|edi_compliance|order_accuracy|return_processing — promote to reference product]
reference: GS1 EDI Standards; NRF Supply Chain KPI Framework; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: The principal quantitative performance target that must be met to satisfy this SLA. For Fill Rate SLAs this is a percentage (e.g., 98.5); for Lead Time SLAs this is a number of days; for EDI Compliance this is a percentage. Interpreted in conjunction with threshold_unit.
reference: NRF Supply Chain KPI Framework; ISO 9001

description: Unit of measure for the target_threshold_value. Percent applies to fill rate and compliance SLAs; Days or Hours apply to lead time and on-time delivery SLAs; Units or Cases apply to volume-based SLAs.
reference: GS1 Unit of Measure Standards; NRF Supply Chain KPI Framework

description: Sequential version number of this SLA definition, incremented each time the SLA terms are renegotiated or amended. Version 1 is the original agreement. Enables historical comparison of SLA terms over time.
reference: ISO 9001 Document Control; NRF Supplier Management Standards

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each SLA performance measurement record. Primary key for the sla_performance data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.

Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Vendor SLA compliance (on-time delivery, fill rate, quality) is tracked under compliance programs. SLA breaches trigger corrective actions, chargebacks, and vendor scorecard impacts requiring complian
Reference to the distribution center or fulfillment facility where this SLA performance is being measured. Supports DC-level SLA reporting.
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS; SAP S/4HANA WM Module

description: Reference to the purchase order associated with this SLA performance record. Applicable for fill rate and on-time delivery SLA measurements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Retail MM Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Reference to the SLA definition record that specifies the contractual commitment being measured. Links to the master SLA catalog.
Reference to the supplier party against whom this SLA performance is being tracked. Supports supplier fill rate compliance monitoring and scorecarding.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Retail MM Module; GS1 Supply Chain Standards

description: The measured actual metric value achieved during the measurement period. For fill rate SLAs this is the actual fill rate percentage achieved. Compared against target_value to determine breach status.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: Indicates whether the actual performance value failed to meet the contractual SLA target for this measurement period. True = SLA breach occurred; False = SLA target met or exceeded. Primary trigger for breach alerting workflows.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: Severity classification of the SLA breach based on the magnitude of variance from target. Critical indicates severe underperformance requiring immediate escalation; none indicates no breach. Used to prioritize corrective action and chargeback processing.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: The monetary value of the vendor compliance chargeback assessed against the supplier for this SLA breach, expressed in the operating currency. Calculated per the contractual chargeback schedule. Applicable only when chargeback_eligible_flag is True.
reference: FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; NRF Vendor Compliance Standards; FTC Pricing Transparency

description: Indicates whether this SLA breach qualifies for a vendor compliance chargeback (Chargeback) under the supplier agreement terms. True = chargeback may be issued; False = breach is not chargeback-eligible (e.g., force majeure, waived). SSOT for chargeback processing workflows.
reference: NRF Vendor Compliance Standards; FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: Current processing status of the vendor compliance chargeback associated with this SLA breach. Pending = not yet issued; issued = chargeback sent to supplier; disputed = supplier has contested; resolved = settled; waived = chargeback forgiven.
reference: FASB ASC 606; NRF Vendor Compliance Standards

description: The number of consecutive measurement periods in which this SLA has been breached by the same supplier, as of this record. Used to identify chronic underperformers and trigger escalation or contract review.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Vendor Compliance Standards

description: The actual date on which the supplier's corrective action plan was confirmed as completed and accepted. Null if corrective action is still in progress or not required.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: The contractually or operationally agreed deadline by which the supplier must submit or complete the corrective action plan for the SLA breach. Used for escalation tracking.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: Status of the corrective action plan (CAP) initiated in response to an SLA breach. Not_required = no breach or waived; pending = CAP requested but not started; in_progress = CAP underway; completed = CAP closed; overdue = CAP past due date.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: The date and time when this SLA performance record was first created in the system. Audit trail field supporting data lineage and compliance requirements.
reference: ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5; CCPA

description: The operational system of record from which the SLA performance data was sourced. Supports data lineage, audit, and reconciliation. SAP_S4HANA = SAP S/4HANA Retail; ORMS = the retail merchandising system Merchandising System; MANHATTAN_WMS = Manhattan Associates WMS; BLUE_YONDER = Blue Yonder Demand Planning; EDI = Electronic Data Interchange feed.

Indicates whether this SLA breach has been escalated to senior management or a formal supplier review process due to severity, recurrence, or overdue corrective action. True = escalated; False = not escalated.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: The supplier fill rate expressed as a decimal percentage, calculated as shipped_quantity divided by ordered_quantity. Represents the Order Completion Percentage (Fill Rate) for this measurement period. Applicable only for fill_rate SLA type.
reference: NRF Supply Chain Standards; GS1 EDI Standards

description: The frequency at which this SLA is measured and reported. Determines the granularity of the measurement_period_start_date and measurement_period_end_date window.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Industry Standards

description: The end date of the measurement window for which this SLA performance record is calculated. Together with measurement_period_start_date defines the SLA evaluation window.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Industry Standards

description: The start date of the measurement window for which this SLA performance record is calculated. Used to define the reporting period for scorecarding and compliance monitoring.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Industry Standards

description: The precise date and time when this SLA performance measurement was captured or calculated. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for this record.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; SAP S/4HANA Retail

description: The unit of measure for the SLA metric values (target_value, actual_value, variance_value). Percentage applies to fill rate and accuracy SLAs; days/hours apply to lead time and on-time delivery SLAs; units/cases apply to quantity-based SLAs.
reference: GS1 Global Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, dispute details, exception justifications, or operational commentary related to this SLA performance record. Used by supply chain analysts and vendor managers.
Total quantity of units or cases ordered on the associated purchase order(s) within the measurement period. Used as the denominator in fill rate percentage calculation for fill rate SLA types.
reference: GS1 Supply Chain Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Current lifecycle status of this SLA performance record. Compliant = target met; breached = target missed; at_risk = approaching threshold; under_review = disputed or under investigation; waived = breach formally excused by agreement.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; SAP S/4HANA Retail

description: Total quantity of units or cases physically received and confirmed at the distribution center within the measurement period. May differ from shipped_quantity due to transit damage or discrepancies.
reference: GS1 Supply Chain Standards; Manhattan Associates WMS

description: The date on which the SLA breach was formally resolved, including completion of corrective actions and/or chargeback settlement. Null for open or compliant records. Used for resolution cycle time reporting.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: The standardized scorecard period label for this SLA measurement, used in supplier performance scorecarding and reporting. Format: YYYY-Qn for quarterly, YYYY-Wnn for weekly, or YYYY-MM for monthly periods.
reference: NRF Vendor Compliance Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Total quantity of units or cases shipped by the supplier against the ordered quantity within the measurement period. Used in fill rate calculation and short-ship analysis.
reference: GS1 Supply Chain Standards; Manhattan Associates WMS

description: The quantity shortfall between ordered_quantity and shipped_quantity. Represents units not fulfilled by the supplier. Used for chargeback calculation and supplier compliance reporting.
reference: NRF Supply Chain Standards; SAP S/4HANA Retail MM Module

description: Standardized reason code explaining why the supplier shipped less than the ordered quantity. Used for root cause analysis, chargeback eligibility determination, and supplier performance improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: out_of_stock|allocation_shortage|production_delay|transportation_delay|order_error|weather_event|force_majeure — promote to reference product]
reference: GS1 EDI Standards; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: Externally-known business identifier for this SLA performance record, used in supplier communications, chargeback documentation, and audit trails. Format: SLA-YYYY-NNNNNN.
reference: GS1 EDI Standards; SAP S/4HANA Retail

description: Classification of the SLA commitment being measured. Fill rate tracks order completion percentage; on_time_delivery tracks delivery punctuality; lead_time tracks supplier delivery duration; order_accuracy tracks shipment correctness; invoice_accuracy tracks billing correctness; chargeback_compliance tracks vendor compliance penalty adherence. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fill_rate|on_time_delivery|lead_time|order_accuracy|invoice_accuracy|chargeback_compliance — promote to reference product]
reference: NRF Supply Chain Standards; GS1 EDI Standards

description: The originating transaction identifier from the source system of record (e.g., SAP delivery document number, EDI 856 ASN number, WMS receipt number) that this SLA performance record is derived from. Supports audit trail and reconciliation.
reference: GS1 EDI Standards; SAP S/4HANA Retail; ISO 27001

description: The contractually agreed target metric value for this SLA commitment. For fill rate SLAs this is the target fill rate percentage (e.g., 0.9500 = 95%). For lead time SLAs this is the target number of days. Unit of measure is defined by sla_type.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: The date and time when this SLA performance record was last modified. Audit trail field used to track corrections, status changes, and chargeback updates.
reference: ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5; CCPA

description: The arithmetic difference between actual_value and target_value (actual minus target). Negative values indicate underperformance against the SLA commitment. Used for trend analysis and breach severity assessment.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Supply Chain Standards

description: Primary key for edi_transaction

The EDI interchange receiver identifier (ISA08) as defined in the interchange control header. Identifies the intended recipient of the EDI transmission. May be the trading partner's EDI ID (outbound) or the retailer's EDI ID (inbound).
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA08 Segment Specification

description: Foreign key linking to product.item_cross_reference. Business justification: EDI document processing (850 PO, 856 ASN) requires mapping trading partner item numbers to internal SKUs. Cross-reference table provides this translation during inbound EDI transaction parsing, enabli

The shipment or ASN reference number extracted from the EDI document payload (e.g., BSN02 on 856 ASN). Links the EDI transaction to the physical shipment record in Manhattan Associates WMS for inbound receiving and cross-docking workflows.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 856 ASN BSN Segment; Manhattan Associates WMS

description: The EDI interchange sender identifier (ISA06) as defined in the interchange control header. Identifies the originating party of the EDI transmission. May be the retailer's EDI ID (outbound) or the trading partner's EDI ID (inbound).
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA06 Segment Specification

description: Surrogate identifier referencing the trading partner (supplier, 3PL, or logistics provider) involved in this EDI transaction. Links to the supplier/trading partner master record for onboarding validation and compliance scoring.
reference: GS1 GLN Standard; ANSI ASC X12; Informatica MDM

description: A numeric score (0.00–100.00) representing the degree of compliance of this EDI transaction against the retailer's routing guide requirements and EDI standards. Calculated by the VAN or integration platform based on segment completeness, data element accuracy, and timing adherence. Drives trading partner scorecards and chargeback assessments.
reference: NRF EDI Routing Guide; GS1 EDI Compliance Framework

description: The date and time when this EDI transaction record was first created in the Silver layer data product. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
reference: ISO 27001 Information Security Management; FASB ASC 606

description: Indicates whether the EDI document was received from a trading partner (INBOUND) or sent to a trading partner (OUTBOUND) by the retailer. Critical for routing guide compliance monitoring and SLA tracking.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: The business document reference number embedded within the EDI transaction, such as the Purchase Order number (850), Invoice number (810), or ASN shipment reference (856). Enables cross-referencing with source documents in SAP S/4HANA MM, the retail merchandising system, or Manhattan WMS.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 BEG/BIG/BSN Segment; GS1 EDI; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: The size of the raw EDI document payload in bytes. Used for VAN transmission cost allocation, integration platform capacity planning, and anomaly detection (e.g., unusually large or empty documents).
reference: GS1 EDI; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: The EDI messaging standard used for this transaction (e.g., ANSI X12 for North American retail, EDIFACT for international trading partners, TRADACOMS for UK retail). Determines parsing rules and compliance validation logic.
reference: GS1 EDI; ANSI ASC X12; UN/EDIFACT ISO 9735

description: The version of the EDI standard used for this transaction (e.g., '004010', '005010', '006020' for ANSI X12; 'D96A', 'D01B' for EDIFACT). Version determines segment and element specifications for validation.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA12 Version Identifier; GS1 EDI

description: The primary error code returned when an EDI transaction fails validation or processing (e.g., ANSI X12 AK304 error codes: 1=Unrecognized segment, 2=Unexpected segment, 3=Mandatory segment missing, 8=Segment has data element errors). Supports error triage and trading partner remediation.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 AK3/AK4 Error Codes; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: Human-readable description of the error or validation failure for this EDI transaction. Provides context for error resolution, trading partner notification, and chargeback dispute management.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 AK3/AK4 Error Codes; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: The acknowledgment status returned in the 997 Functional Acknowledgment or 999 Implementation Acknowledgment for this transaction. Indicates whether the trading partner accepted, accepted with errors, or rejected the EDI document. Critical for EDI compliance monitoring and chargeback prevention.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 997/999 Transaction Set; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: The date and time when the 997 Functional Acknowledgment was received for this transaction. Used to calculate acknowledgment turnaround time and detect SLA breaches for late acknowledgments per retailer routing guide requirements.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 997 Transaction Set; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: The control number assigned to the functional group (GS06 segment) within the EDI interchange. Groups related transaction sets of the same type and enables functional acknowledgment (997) matching at the group level.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 GS06 Segment Specification

description: The unique 9-digit control number assigned to the EDI interchange envelope (ISA13 segment). Used to uniquely identify and track each interchange transmission for deduplication, acknowledgment matching, and audit purposes.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA13 Segment Specification

description: The supplier invoice number extracted from the EDI 810 Invoice transaction payload (BIG02 segment). Used to match EDI invoices against purchase orders and receipts in SAP S/4HANA FI/CO for three-way match and accounts payable processing.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 810 Invoice BIG Segment; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; FASB ASC 606

description: The date and time when the EDI transaction was fully processed and accepted or rejected by the downstream system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA MM, the retail merchandising system). Used to measure end-to-end processing latency and SLA adherence.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 997 Functional Acknowledgment; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: Current processing lifecycle state of the EDI transaction within the VAN/integration platform. Drives SLA breach detection, retry workflows, and integration health dashboards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: RECEIVED|QUEUED|PROCESSING|ACCEPTED|REJECTED|ERROR|RETRYING|ACKNOWLEDGED — promote to reference product]
reference: ANSI ASC X12 997 Functional Acknowledgment; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: The retailer's Purchase Order number associated with this EDI transaction, extracted from the document payload (e.g., BEG02 on 850, BIG04 on 810, BSN02 on 856). Enables cross-referencing with SAP S/4HANA MM purchase orders and the retail merchandising system procurement records.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 BEG/BIG/BSN Segment; SAP S/4HANA MM; Oracle RMS

description: The date and time when the EDI document was received and ingested by the retailer's integration platform or VAN. Used to calculate transmission latency and inbound SLA compliance windows.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Interchange Control Header; NRF EDI Routing Guide

description: The number of times this EDI transaction has been retried after an initial failure or rejection. Used to identify persistently failing transactions, trigger escalation workflows, and monitor integration platform health.

The version of the retailer's EDI routing guide against which this transaction was validated (e.g., 'v2024.1'). Enables compliance scoring to be evaluated against the correct version of requirements, supporting trading partner onboarding and annual routing guide updates.
reference: NRF EDI Routing Guide; GS1 EDI Compliance Framework

description: The total number of segments in the EDI transaction set as reported in the SE02 trailer segment. Used for document integrity validation — the received segment count must match the SE02 value to confirm complete transmission.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 SE02 Transaction Set Trailer; GS1 EDI

description: Indicates whether this EDI transaction breached the retailer's routing guide SLA requirement (True = SLA breached, False = within SLA). Populated based on comparison of transmission_timestamp against sla_target_hours. Drives SLA breach alerts and chargeback workflows.
reference: NRF EDI Routing Guide; FTC Advertising Standards

business_glossary_term: EDI Service Level Agreement (SLA) Target Hours
description: The contractual SLA target in hours within which this EDI transaction type must be transmitted and acknowledged per the retailer's routing guide (e.g., ASN must be sent within 24 hours of shipment). Used as the benchmark for SLA breach detection.
reference: NRF EDI Routing Guide; SLA Definition

description: Indicates whether the EDI interchange is a test transmission (T) or a production transmission (P) as specified in the ISA15 segment. Test transactions must be excluded from operational processing and compliance scoring.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA15 Segment Specification

business_glossary_term: Trading Partner Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number
description: The Dun & Bradstreet DUNS number of the trading partner, a 9-digit identifier used for supplier identity verification, credit risk assessment, and EDI partner onboarding validation.
reference: Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Standard; ANSI ASC X12 ISA Interchange Header

description: The GS1 Global Location Number (GLN) of the trading partner (supplier, 3PL, or DC) involved in this EDI exchange. A 13-digit GS1 identifier used to uniquely identify legal entities and physical locations in the supply chain. Required for GS1-compliant EDI routing.
reference: GS1 GLN Standard; GS1 EDI; NRF EDI Guidelines

description: The registered business name of the trading partner (supplier, 3PL, or logistics provider) as maintained in the EDI partner profile. Supports human-readable reporting and onboarding dashboards.
reference: Informatica MDM; GS1 EDI Partner Profile

description: The ANSI X12 ISA qualifier code indicating the type of trading partner identifier used in the interchange (e.g., 01=DUNS, 08=UCC EDI Comm ID, 12=Phone, 14=DUNS+4, 20=Health Industry Number, ZZ=Mutually Defined). Required for EDI interchange routing.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Segment Specification; GS1 EDI

description: The control number assigned to the individual transaction set (ST02 segment) within the functional group. Uniquely identifies a single transaction set for acknowledgment and error tracking.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ST02 Segment Specification

description: The ANSI X12 or EDIFACT transaction set number identifying the document type exchanged (e.g., 850 Purchase Order, 855 PO Acknowledgment, 856 Advance Ship Notice, 810 Invoice, 860 PO Change Order, 997 Functional Acknowledgment, 832 Price/Sales Catalog, 846 Inventory Inquiry). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 850|855|856|810|860|997|832|846|753|754 — promote to reference product]
reference: ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards; GS1 EDI; NRF EDI Guidelines

description: Human-readable name of the EDI transaction set type (e.g., 'Purchase Order', 'Advance Ship Notice (ASN)', 'Invoice', 'Functional Acknowledgment') corresponding to the transaction_set_id. Supports dashboards and reporting without requiring code lookups.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards; GS1 EDI

description: The communication protocol used to transmit the EDI document (e.g., AS2, SFTP, FTP, HTTPS, VAN mailbox, AS4). Relevant for integration health dashboards and security compliance audits per ISO 27001.
reference: ANSI ASC X12; AS2 RFC 4130; ISO 27001

description: The date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the EDI document was transmitted over the VAN or direct connection. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for SLA measurement and audit trails.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Interchange Control Header; GS1 EDI

description: The date and time when this EDI transaction record was last modified in the Silver layer data product, such as when processing status changed or retry count incremented.

The Value-Added Network (VAN) or direct EDI integration provider used to transmit this transaction (e.g., SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce, Sterling Commerce, OpenText, Direct AS2/SFTP). Supports integration health monitoring and VAN cost allocation.
reference: NRF EDI Routing Guide; GS1 EDI

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each SKU-level demand forecast record generated by Blue Yonder Demand Planning. Serves as the primary key for this table.
add column financial_period_id (BIGINT) with FK to finance.financial_period.financial_period_id - forecasts align to financial periods for budget integration
Reference to the store, distribution center (DC), or fulfillment node for which the demand forecast applies. Supports store-level and DC-level replenishment planning.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) — Location Management

description: add column merchandising_category_id (BIGINT) with FK to merchandising.category.category_id - demand forecasts are generated at category level in addition to SKU level for aggregate planning

Foreign key linking to workforce.associate. Business justification: Demand planners own forecasts for planning accountability and accuracy tracking. Supply chain tracks planner MAPE, bias, and forecast quality by planner for performance management, S&OP reviews, and p
Reference to the specific Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) for which the demand forecast is generated. The SKU is the atomic unit of inventory and demand planning in retail.
reference: GS1 — Global Product Classification; Informatica MDM — Product Golden Record

description: The pure statistical baseline demand forecast in units before any adjustments for promotions, seasonality, or manual overrides. Provides the unadjusted demand signal for comparison against the final consensus forecast.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Baseline Demand Signal

description: The statistical confidence level (expressed as a percentage, e.g., 95.00) associated with the forecast interval. Indicates the probability that actual demand will fall within the forecast range. Used to set safety stock levels and replenishment buffers.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Probabilistic Forecasting; NRF — Inventory Optimization Standards

description: The timestamp when this demand forecast record was first written to the Silver Layer lakehouse. Supports data lineage, audit trails, and incremental load processing.
reference: ISO 27001 — Information Security Management; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the forecasted revenue amount (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Supports multi-currency retail operations across international markets.
reference: ISO 4217 — Currency Codes; FASB — Financial Reporting Standards

description: The operational system of record that provided the demand signal inputs used to generate this forecast (e.g., SAP_CAR for POS transaction data, the e-commerce platform_Commerce_Cloud for e-commerce demand, ORMS for inventory positions). Supports data lineage and source system auditability.
reference: SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); Informatica MDM — Data Lineage; ISO 27001 — Information Security

description: Classification of the SKU's demand pattern used to select the appropriate forecasting model. 'regular' indicates stable, predictable demand; 'intermittent' indicates sporadic demand (Croston model); 'lumpy' indicates irregular high-volume spikes; 'new_item' indicates insufficient history; 'end_of_life' indicates declining/discontinuing SKU.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Demand Classification; NRF — Assortment Planning Standards

description: The systematic directional error in the forecast, calculated as the mean of (forecasted units minus actual units) over a rolling period. Positive values indicate over-forecasting (excess inventory risk); negative values indicate under-forecasting (stockout risk). Critical for replenishment safety stock calibration.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Bias Analysis; NRF — Inventory Planning Standards

description: The exact date and time when this forecast record was generated by the Blue Yonder Demand Planning engine. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for the forecast lifecycle and supports version comparison across planning cycles.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Run Audit

description: The total number of weeks into the future covered by this forecast run, measured from the forecast generation date. Determines the planning horizon for replenishment, Open-to-Buy (OTB), and supply chain optimization.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Horizon Configuration; NRF — Supply Chain Planning Standards

description: The lower bound of the forecast confidence interval in units at the specified confidence level. Represents the low-demand scenario used for minimum order quantity (MOQ) planning and markdown risk assessment.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Probabilistic Forecast Intervals

description: The last calendar date of the forecast horizon period covered by this record. Together with forecast_period_start_date, defines the time bucket granularity (daily, weekly, monthly).
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Horizon Configuration

description: The first calendar date of the forecast horizon period covered by this record. Defines the beginning of the time bucket (day, week, or month) for which demand is forecasted.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Horizon Configuration

description: Identifier for the specific Blue Yonder Demand Planning batch run that generated this forecast record. Enables traceability back to the originating planning cycle and supports audit of forecast lineage.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Run Management

description: Current lifecycle state of the demand forecast record. 'draft' indicates a preliminary run; 'published' indicates the forecast is active for replenishment; 'approved' indicates planner sign-off; 'overridden' indicates a manual adjustment was applied; 'superseded' indicates a newer run has replaced this record; 'archived' indicates the record is retained for historical analysis only.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Workflow; NRF — Demand Planning Best Practices

description: Classification of the demand forecast by its planning purpose. 'baseline' is the statistical base demand without uplift; 'promotional' incorporates promotion lift; 'seasonal' reflects seasonal index adjustments; 'event_driven' accounts for specific demand events; 'consensus' is the final agreed forecast used for replenishment and Open-to-Buy (OTB) planning.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Type Configuration; NRF — Demand Planning Standards

description: The upper bound of the forecast confidence interval in units at the specified confidence level. Represents the high-demand scenario used for safety stock and maximum inventory planning to prevent stockouts.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Probabilistic Forecast Intervals

description: An incrementing integer version number for the forecast record for a given SKU-location-period combination. Enables tracking of forecast revisions across planning cycles and supports comparison of forecast evolution over time.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Versioning; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: The projected revenue in the operating currency derived from the forecasted units multiplied by the expected selling price for the forecast period. Used in financial planning, Open-to-Buy (OTB) budgeting, and Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) analysis.
reference: FASB ASC 606 — Revenue Recognition; Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Financial Forecast Output

description: The statistical model's predicted demand quantity in sellable units for the SKU at the specified location during the forecast period. This is the primary quantitative output of the demand planning engine and drives replenishment order quantities.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Demand Signal Output; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) — Replenishment Planning

description: Indicates whether this forecast record is the most current version for the given SKU-location-period combination. True means this record is the active forecast used for replenishment and OTB planning; False means it has been superseded by a newer forecast run.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Version Management; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Indicates whether the SKU is a new item with insufficient sales history for statistical forecasting. When True, the forecast relies on analogous item modeling or planner input rather than historical demand patterns. Relevant for new product launches and assortment introductions.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) — New Item Setup; Blue Yonder Demand Planning — New Item Forecasting

description: Indicates whether a demand planner has manually overridden the statistical forecast for this record. True means the final forecasted_units reflect a planner adjustment; False means the forecast is purely statistical. Critical for measuring forecast bias introduced by manual intervention.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Planner Override Workflow; NRF — Demand Planning Governance

description: Indicates whether the forecast period overlaps with an active promotional event. When True, the promotional_lift_units field is expected to be populated and the forecast incorporates promotion-driven demand uplift.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Promotion Calendar; Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Promotion Integration

description: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) measuring the accuracy of the statistical forecast against actual sales for the equivalent prior period. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.12 = 12% error). Lower values indicate higher forecast accuracy. Used as the primary KPI for demand planning performance.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Accuracy Metrics; NRF — Supply Chain KPI Standards

description: The version identifier of the statistical forecasting model used to generate this forecast record. Supports model governance, reproducibility, and performance tracking across model upgrades in Blue Yonder Demand Planning.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Model Versioning; ISO 9001 — Quality Management

description: Indicates whether this forecast record has been incorporated into the Open-to-Buy (OTB) financial plan. When True, the forecasted revenue and units are reflected in the merchandise financial plan and buying budget for the relevant period.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) — Open-to-Buy Planning; NRF — Merchandise Financial Planning Standards

description: A standardized code indicating the business reason for the planner's manual override of the statistical forecast (e.g., new product launch, competitor action, supply constraint, market intelligence). Populated only when is_override_applied is True. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NEW_PRODUCT|COMPETITOR_ACTION|SUPPLY_CONSTRAINT|MARKET_INTEL|PROMO_CHANGE|STORE_EVENT|WEATHER — promote to reference product]
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Override Reason Taxonomy; NRF — Demand Planning Standards

description: The manually adjusted demand quantity in units entered by a demand planner to replace or supplement the statistical forecast. Populated only when is_override_applied is True. Enables analysis of planner override magnitude and its impact on forecast accuracy.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Planner Override; NRF — Demand Planning Governance

description: The retail fulfillment channel for which this demand forecast is generated. 'store' covers brick-and-mortar POS demand; 'ecommerce' covers digital commerce demand from the e-commerce platform; 'omnichannel' covers unified demand signals; 'dc_replenishment' covers distribution center stock replenishment; 'bopis' covers Buy Online Pick Up In Store (BOPIS) demand.
reference: SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR) — Unified Demand Signals; Salesforce Commerce Cloud — Digital Demand; NRF — Omnichannel Standards

description: The incremental demand units attributed to active promotions during the forecast period. Derived from promotion event modeling in Blue Yonder and used to isolate the promotional demand signal from baseline demand for Pricing and Promotions Management analysis.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Promotion Lift Modeling; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: The system-recommended replenishment order quantity in units derived from the demand forecast, current inventory position, safety stock targets, and lead time. Feeds directly into the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS) purchase order generation and Open-to-Buy (OTB) planning.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Replenishment Optimization; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) — Purchase Order Management

description: A multiplicative seasonal index applied to the baseline forecast to account for recurring seasonal demand patterns (e.g., holiday peaks, back-to-school). A value of 1.0 indicates no seasonal adjustment; values above 1.0 indicate above-average seasonal demand.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Seasonal Decomposition; NRF — Seasonal Planning Standards

description: The identifier or code of the statistical forecasting algorithm used by Blue Yonder Demand Planning to generate this forecast (e.g., ARIMA, Holt-Winters exponential smoothing, Croston for intermittent demand, machine learning ensemble). Enables model performance benchmarking and algorithm governance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ARIMA|HOLT_WINTERS|CROSTON|ETS|MOVING_AVG|ML_ENSEMBLE|CAUSAL — promote to reference product]
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Model Library; NRF — Demand Forecasting Best Practices

description: The temporal granularity of the forecast period covered by this record. 'daily' is used for short-horizon replenishment; 'weekly' is the standard planning cadence; 'monthly' is used for financial and Open-to-Buy (OTB) planning.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Planning Calendar Configuration

description: A multiplicative factor representing the long-term demand trend applied to the forecast. Values above 1.0 indicate upward trend; values below 1.0 indicate declining demand trend. Used to capture secular demand shifts beyond seasonal patterns.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Trend Component; NRF — Demand Planning Best Practices

description: The timestamp when this demand forecast record was last modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse, including override applications, accuracy recalculations, or status changes.
reference: ISO 27001 — Information Security Management; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Weeks of Supply (WOS) — the projected number of weeks the current on-hand inventory will cover demand based on the forecasted units. A key inventory health metric used in replenishment planning to identify stockout risk and excess inventory positions.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Replenishment Planning; NRF — Inventory Management KPIs

description: Weighted Mean Absolute Percentage Error (WMAPE) measuring forecast accuracy weighted by sales volume, reducing the distortion caused by low-volume SKUs. Expressed as a decimal. Preferred accuracy metric for high-volume retail assortments where MAPE can be misleading.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning — Forecast Accuracy Metrics; NRF — Supply Chain KPI Standards

description: Primary key for plan
Reference to the Distribution Center (DC) for which this supply plan is generated. Identifies the fulfillment node responsible for receiving, storing, and distributing the planned SKU.

Reference to an active promotion associated with this SKU-DC-week supply plan. Promotional events drive demand uplift adjustments to the consensus demand quantity and may require incremental supply planning.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Promotions Management Best Practices

description: Reference to the open Purchase Order (PO) associated with this supply plan record. Links the plan to the procurement execution layer for tracking open PO quantities and expected receipt dates.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Reference to the specific Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) being planned. The SKU is the lowest-level product identifier used for inventory tracking and replenishment planning.
reference: GS1 Global Product Classification; NRF MDM Standards

description: Reference to the primary supplier responsible for fulfilling the planned receipt quantities for this SKU-DC combination. Used to evaluate supplier capacity constraints during supply-demand balancing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; EDI Standards

description: Numeric rank (1 = highest priority) assigned to this DC for allocation of constrained supply for the SKU. Used by planners to prioritize distribution of limited inventory across DCs and stores during supply-constrained periods.
reference: NRF Allocation and Replenishment Best Practices; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Approval workflow status of the supply plan record within the S&OP governance process. Pending plans await planner or manager sign-off; approved plans are authorized for execution; rejected plans require revision; escalated plans require senior leadership review.
Date and time when the supply plan record was approved in the S&OP workflow. Provides a precise audit trail for plan authorization and supports compliance with internal governance controls.
reference: NRF S&OP Governance Best Practices; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Name or employee identifier of the supply chain planner or manager who approved this supply plan record in the S&OP workflow. Provides audit trail for plan authorization decisions.
reference: NRF S&OP Governance Best Practices; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Projected on-hand inventory quantity for the SKU at the DC at the start of the planning week, before any receipts or demand consumption. Used as the opening inventory position for supply-demand balancing calculations.
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Agreed demand quantity after S&OP consensus adjustments, incorporating planner overrides, promotional uplifts, and commercial inputs. This is the demand signal used for supply-demand balancing in the approved plan.
reference: NRF S&OP Best Practices; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

description: Date and time when this supply plan record was first created in the system. Provides the audit trail creation marker for the plan lifecycle and supports data lineage tracking in the Silver layer.
reference: ISO 8000 Data Quality Standards; ISO 27001 Information Security

description: Quantity of the SKU planned for cross-docking at the DC, bypassing put-away storage and flowing directly from inbound receipt to outbound shipment. Supports DC throughput optimization and reduces handling costs for high-velocity items.
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS; NRF Distribution Center Operations Best Practices

description: Statistical demand forecast quantity for the SKU at the DC for the planning week, expressed in the SKU's unit of measure. Sourced from Blue Yonder Demand Planning and represents the baseline demand signal before supply constraints are applied.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

description: Indicates whether the projected on-hand quantity exceeds the maximum inventory target for the SKU-DC combination in the planning week. When True, signals a potential dead stock or overstock situation requiring markdown or redistribution action.
reference: NRF Inventory Management Best Practices; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Quantity of the SKU currently in transit from supplier or another DC, expected to arrive at the destination DC within the planning week. Represents confirmed supply pipeline inventory not yet received.
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS; SAP S/4HANA WM Module

description: Maximum allowable on-hand inventory quantity for the SKU at the DC, representing the upper bound of the inventory target range. Projected on-hand quantities exceeding this threshold trigger the excess inventory flag.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ) required by the supplier for this SKU, representing the smallest quantity that can be ordered in a single purchase order. Constrains replenishment order quantities in the supply plan.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Quantity on open, unfulfilled Purchase Orders (POs) for this SKU-DC combination expected to be received within the planning week. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA MM and ORMS to represent committed supply.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Business-facing externally-known identifier for the supply plan record, used in S&OP communications, planner workflows, and cross-system references. Typically formatted as a combination of DC code, SKU, and planning week.
reference: NRF Supply Chain Planning Best Practices; GS1 Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the supply plan record within the S&OP approval workflow. Draft plans are under construction; submitted plans await approval; approved plans are baselined for execution; locked plans are frozen for the current cycle.
reference: NRF S&OP Best Practices; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

description: Classification of the supply plan by planning methodology. Consensus plans reflect agreed S&OP output; unconstrained plans reflect pure demand signal; constrained plans incorporate supplier and DC capacity limits; allocation plans reflect prioritized distribution of limited supply.
reference: NRF S&OP Best Practices; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

description: Total quantity of the SKU planned to be received at the DC during the planning week from all supply sources (open POs, in-transit, cross-dock). Core output of the supply planning process used to assess coverage against demand.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); SAP S/4HANA MM Module

description: Free-text notes entered by the supply chain planner to document assumptions, exceptions, override rationale, or action items associated with this supply plan record. Supports S&OP review discussions and audit trail.
Number of weeks forward from the plan week start date that this supply plan covers. Defines the rolling planning window used for demand-supply balancing and replenishment trigger decisions.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; NRF Supply Chain Planning Best Practices

description: Projected ending on-hand inventory quantity for the SKU at the DC at the end of the planning week, calculated as beginning on-hand plus planned receipts minus consensus demand. Key metric for identifying coverage gaps and excess inventory.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Incremental demand quantity attributed to a promotional event for this SKU-DC-week, added on top of the baseline statistical forecast to derive the consensus demand quantity. Sourced from the promotions planning system.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Blue Yonder Demand Planning

description: Recommended replenishment order quantity for the SKU-DC combination for the planning week, calculated by the planning system to bring projected on-hand to the target inventory level. Serves as the basis for generating new purchase orders.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Minimum buffer inventory quantity required for the SKU at the DC to protect against demand variability and supply uncertainty. Serves as the replenishment trigger threshold in the supply plan.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; NRF Inventory Management Best Practices

description: Percentage of available inventory for this SKU that has been sold within the planning period, calculated as units sold divided by beginning inventory plus receipts. Used to assess demand velocity and identify slow-moving or dead stock.
reference: NRF Inventory Performance KPIs; SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this supply plan record originated. Enables data lineage tracking and reconciliation between planning systems. Values include BLUE_YONDER (Blue Yonder Demand Planning), SAP_S4 (SAP S/4HANA), ORMS (the retail merchandising system Merchandising System), or MANUAL (planner-entered).

Quantitative risk score (0-100) indicating the probability of a stockout event for the SKU at the DC within the planning horizon. Derived from demand variability, supply reliability, and projected on-hand versus safety stock. Used to prioritize replenishment actions.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; NRF Supply Chain Risk Management

description: Historical fill rate percentage for this supplier-SKU combination, representing the percentage of ordered quantity actually delivered on time. Used as a supply reliability input to safety stock and risk score calculations.
reference: NRF Supplier Performance Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM Module

description: Number of days from purchase order placement to expected receipt at the DC for this SKU-supplier combination. Used in replenishment planning to determine order timing and assess supply pipeline coverage.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; GS1 Supply Chain Standards

description: Indicates whether the supply plan for this SKU-DC-week is constrained by supplier capacity, lead time, or minimum order quantity (MOQ) limitations. When True, planned receipt quantity is below unconstrained demand, triggering allocation prioritization.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; SAP S/4HANA MM Module

description: Unit of measure in which all quantity fields (demand, receipt, on-hand) are expressed for this SKU in the supply plan. Common values include EA (each), CS (case), PK (pack). Ensures consistent quantity interpretation across planning systems. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|PK|LB|KG|OZ|L|M — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: GS1 Global Standards; ISO 80000 Quantities and Units

description: Date and time when this supply plan record was last modified, including planner overrides, system recalculations, or status changes. Supports change tracking and version management in the S&OP process.
reference: ISO 8000 Data Quality Standards; ISO 27001 Information Security

description: Sequential version number of the supply plan, incremented each time the plan is revised within the same planning cycle. Enables planners to track plan evolution and compare versions during S&OP reviews.
reference: NRF Supply Chain Planning Best Practices

description: The last day (Sunday) of the planning week for which this supply plan record applies. Used in conjunction with plan_week_start_date to define the weekly planning horizon bucket.

description: The first day (Monday) of the planning week for which this supply plan record applies. Defines the weekly time bucket used in S&OP reviews and demand-supply balancing at the SKU-DC-week granularity.
reference: NRF Retail Calendar Standards; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

description: Weeks of Supply (WOS) metric representing the number of weeks the projected on-hand inventory can cover at the current consensus demand rate. A key S&OP KPI used to identify stockout risk and excess inventory positions.
reference: NRF Supply Chain KPI Standards; Blue Yonder Demand Planning

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each replenishment plan record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for the replenishment_plan data product.
reference: ISO/IEC 11179 - Data Element Naming and Definition

description: Reference to the demand forecast plan from Blue Yonder Demand Planning that drove the generation of this replenishment plan. Enables traceability from replenishment decision back to the underlying demand signal.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning - Demand Plan Reference

description: Reference to the supply chain node (store, Distribution Center (DC), or Micro-Fulfillment Center (MFC)) for which this replenishment plan is generated. Identifies the destination receiving location in the replenishment network.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning - Network Node; Manhattan Associates WMS

Reference to the specific SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) for which this replenishment plan is generated. The SKU is the primary product-level identifier used in replenishment planning across stores, DCs, and MFCs.
reference: GS1 - Global Product Identification Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Reference to the primary supplier responsible for fulfilling this replenishment plan. Links to the supplier master for MOQ enforcement, lead time, and EDI ordering constraints.

description: The final order quantity approved by the buyer or auto-approved by the system after MOQ, order multiple, and buyer override adjustments. This is the quantity that will be transmitted to the supplier via EDI or purchase order.

description: Indicates whether a buyer has manually overridden the system-generated planned order quantity or parameters. True = buyer override applied; False = system-generated values accepted as-is. Supports audit trail for manual interventions.

description: Audit timestamp recording when this replenishment plan record was first persisted in the Silver layer lakehouse. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
reference: ISO 27001 - Information Security Management; FASB ASC 606

description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the planned order value and unit cost are expressed (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Required for multi-currency retail operations.

The quantity of the SKU physically on hand at the supply node at the time the replenishment plan was generated. Sourced from Manhattan Associates WMS or SAP S/4HANA WM. Used as the starting inventory position for plan calculations.
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS - On-Hand Inventory; SAP S/4HANA WM Module

description: A statistical measure of demand variability (coefficient of variation or standard deviation of demand) used by the planning engine to size safety stock. Higher values indicate more volatile demand and result in larger safety stock buffers.

description: The target order fill rate percentage (Fill Rate) for this replenishment plan, representing the percentage of demand that should be fulfilled from available inventory. Used as a supply chain performance KPI (KPI) target for this SKU-node combination.

description: The total forecasted demand quantity for the SKU at the supply node over the plan horizon, as generated by Blue Yonder Demand Planning. The primary input to the planned order quantity calculation.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning - Demand Forecast; SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

description: The number of calendar days from purchase order placement to expected receipt at the supply node, as defined in the supplier contract or purchasing info record. Used to calculate reorder points and plan order release dates.

description: The minimum monetary value of a purchase order required by the supplier, expressed in the operating currency. Replenishment plans that do not meet the minimum order value threshold are consolidated or flagged for buyer action.

description: The minimum number of units that must be ordered from the supplier per purchase order line, as enforced by supplier contract terms. Replenishment plans with planned_order_qty below MOQ are rounded up or flagged for buyer review.

description: Indicates whether the planned order quantity meets or exceeds the supplier's Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ) constraint. True = compliant; False = below MOQ threshold and requires buyer review or order consolidation before release.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - MOQ Validation; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Classifies the type of supply chain node receiving the replenishment. Values: store (retail store), dc (Distribution Center), mfc (Micro-Fulfillment Center), dark_store (fulfillment-only location). Drives replenishment logic and lead time parameters.

description: The quantity of the SKU already on open purchase orders or in-transit to the supply node at the time of plan generation. Included in the net inventory position calculation to avoid over-ordering.

description: The unit increment in which the SKU must be ordered (e.g., case pack size, pallet quantity). Planned order quantities are rounded up to the nearest order multiple before purchase order generation.

description: The date and time when the replenishment plan was generated by the planning engine (Blue Yonder or equivalent). Represents the principal business event timestamp for this transaction. Used for plan freshness assessment and demand signal alignment.

description: The end date of the planning horizon covered by this replenishment plan. Defines the end of the demand forecast window. Together with plan_horizon_start_date, bounds the coverage period for this plan.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning - Planning Horizon; SAP S/4HANA MM - Planning Period

description: The start date of the planning horizon covered by this replenishment plan. Defines the beginning of the demand forecast window used to generate the planned order quantity.

description: Externally-known business identifier for the replenishment plan, generated by Blue Yonder Demand Planning or SAP S/4HANA MM module. Used for cross-system traceability and supplier communication.

description: Current lifecycle state of the replenishment plan within the planning and execution workflow. Drives automated ordering triggers and buyer review queues. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|proposed|approved|released|in_progress|completed|cancelled — promote to reference product]

description: The target in-stock service level percentage used to calculate safety stock and replenishment parameters. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 95.00 = 95%). Represents the probability of not experiencing a stockout during the replenishment lead time.

description: The date and time when this recovery workflow execution record was first created in the data platform. RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.

description: Device type used by the customer when they clicked the recovery link and returned to the storefront. Supports device-level Conversion Rate (CR) analysis and mobile-first optimization decisions.

description: Indicates whether this record represents the first recovery message sent for the associated abandoned cart. True = first attempt; False = subsequent attempt in a multi-touch sequence. Supports first-touch vs. multi-touch attribution analysis.

description: The date and time when the customer opened or viewed the recovery message. Null if the message was not opened. Supports open-rate and engagement analysis by channel and template.

description: Total discount or markdown amount applied to the recovered order, including any recovery-specific promotional incentive. Null when no recovery occurred. MONETARY_TRIPLET adjustment component.

description: The outreach channel used to deliver the cart recovery message to the customer. Drives channel effectiveness measurement and Click-Through Rate (CTR) and Conversion Rate (CR) analysis by channel.

description: The date and time after which the recovery workflow for this cart is considered expired and no further recovery attempts will be made. Determined by campaign configuration (e.g., 72 hours after abandonment). Used to manage recovery window and transition status to 'expired'.

description: Ordinal position of this recovery message within a multi-touch recovery campaign sequence for the same abandoned cart (e.g., 1 = first reminder, 2 = second reminder with incentive, 3 = final expiry notice). Supports multi-touch attribution and sequence effectiveness analysis.

description: Current lifecycle state of the abandoned cart recovery workflow execution. LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.

description: Externally-known business identifier for this recovery workflow execution, as generated by the marketing automation platform (e.g., the e-commerce platform, Braze). Used for cross-system traceability and campaign reporting. BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.

description: Reference to the digital storefront or site context in which this cart was created. The date and time when the cart was classified as abandoned, either by session timeout or explicit inactivity threshold breach. Null for non-abandoned carts. Used to calculate time-to-abandonment metrics, trigger abandoned cart recovery email sequences, and measure recovery window effectiveness.

description: Human-readable, externally referenceable business identifier for the cart instance.
