description: Unique surrogate identifier for each SKU-to-price-list-to-zone-to-channel binding record. Primary key of the sku_price data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: Informatica MDM — Golden Record Key Convention

description: Foreign key linking to pricing.cost_price. Business justification: SKU retail prices are based on cost prices for margin calculation. Adding cost_price_id FK links retail price to authoritative cost record. Removes cost_price DECIMAL as redundant with cost_price.land

Foreign key linking to compliance.food_safety_plan. Business justification: Food SKU pricing in stores/DCs with food safety plans must comply with plan requirements (temperature-controlled storage costs, HACCP-compliant handling). Prices reference applicable food safety plan.

Foreign key linking to compliance.license_permit. Business justification: Regulated SKUs (alcohol, tobacco, pharmacy) require valid licenses to price/sell. Pricing systems validate license status before activating prices; expired licenses block price changes.
Reference to the price list under which this SKU price is governed. Supports multi-list resolution priority for EDLP, Hi-Lo, promotional, and clearance price lists.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price List Entity

description: Reference to the geographic or competitive price zone in which this price applies. Price zones enable regional pricing differentiation across store clusters and markets.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Zone Entity

description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: SKU prices are tracked by profit center for item-level profitability analysis and revenue recognition. Business process: margin analysis and financial performance reporting at store/channel level for

Foreign key linking to promotion.promo_offer. Business justification: Promotional offers define temporary price adjustments at SKU level. Retailers must link offer mechanics to SKU price records to calculate promotional pricing, validate discount limits, and reconcile v

Foreign key linking to pricing.pricing_rule. Business justification: SKU prices may be calculated or adjusted by pricing rules (e.g., dynamic pricing rules, competitive response rules). Adding pricing_rule_id FK tracks which rule generated or last adjusted the price.
Reference to the product SKU for which this price record applies. Resolves to the canonical product master in the Product domain.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) — Item Master; GS1 GTIN Standard

description: Workflow approval status of this price record within the the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) pricing governance process. Only records in 'approved' status are eligible for price resolution at POS and digital channels.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Event Status; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Username or employee identifier of the pricing manager who approved this price record in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM). Required for price change audit trail and SOX compliance.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Approved By; ISO 27001 Access Control; FASB SOX Compliance

description: The date and time at which this price record was approved by the pricing manager. Part of the price change audit trail required for regulatory compliance and pricing governance.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Approval Timestamp; ISO 27001; FASB SOX Compliance

description: The absolute price difference between this channel-specific price and the base in-store retail price for the same SKU, price list, and zone. Quantifies omnichannel price differentiation (e.g., e-commerce price vs. in-store price).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Channel Price Variance; FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: Business justification for any price variance between this channel price and the base retail price. Required for compliance with FTC pricing transparency guidelines and internal pricing governance. Examples: 'Online-only promotion', 'Marketplace fee offset', 'BOPIS incentive'.
reference: FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Event Notes

description: The retail channel for which this price applies. Supports omnichannel price resolution across in-store Point of Sale (POS), e-commerce, mobile app, marketplace, and Buy Online Pick Up In Store (BOPIS) channels.
reference: NRF Omnichannel Retail Standards; Salesforce Commerce Cloud — Channel Configuration

description: The competitor's observed price for this SKU that triggered a competitive match pricing action. Captured when price_type = 'competitive_match'. Supports competitive pricing analytics and price index reporting.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Competitive Price; FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: Name of the competitor whose price was used as the reference for a competitive match pricing action. Populated when price_type = 'competitive_match'. Used in competitive pricing intelligence reporting.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Competitor Reference; FTC Advertising Standards

description: The date and time at which this SKU price record was first created in the Silver Layer data product. Part of the price change audit trail and data lineage tracking.
reference: ISO 27001 Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity; FASB SOX Compliance

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary price fields in this record (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Supports multi-currency retail operations across international markets.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FASB ASC 830 Foreign Currency

description: The calendar date on which this SKU price becomes active and valid for use at Point of Sale (POS) and digital channels. Supports bi-temporal price management and scheduled price changes.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Effective Date; FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: The calendar date on which this SKU price record expires and is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended price with no scheduled expiry. Used for Hi-Lo promotional price windows and clearance event management.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — End Date; NRF Promotional Pricing Standards

description: Current gross margin percentage for this SKU at the current retail price, accounting for any markdowns applied. Calculated as (retail_price - cost_price) / retail_price * 100. Drives GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) reporting.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Margin%; FASB ASC 606; NRF GMROI Standards

description: The Initial Markup (IMU) percentage calculated as (retail_price - cost_price) / retail_price * 100. Represents the planned gross margin at the time of price setting before any markdowns.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — IMU%; NRF Retail Margin Standards

description: Indicates whether dynamic pricing rules are active for this SKU in this price list, zone, and channel context. When True, the price may be algorithmically adjusted within price_floor and price_ceiling bounds based on demand signals from SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Dynamic Pricing Flag; NRF Dynamic Pricing Standards

description: Indicates whether this price record is locked and protected from automated price changes or markdown optimization algorithms. When True, the price can only be changed through a manual approval workflow in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Lock Flag; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: The absolute currency amount by which the original retail price has been reduced (markdown). Markdown = original_retail_price - retail_price. Used for markdown optimization and P&L (Profit and Loss) reporting.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Markdown Amount; NRF Markdown Management Standards

description: The percentage reduction from the original retail price to the current retail price. Markdown% = (original_retail_price - retail_price) / original_retail_price * 100. Supports markdown depth analysis and clearance optimization.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Markdown%; NRF Pricing Standards

description: The Minimum Advertised Price (MAP) floor set by the supplier or brand for this SKU. The retail_price must not be advertised below this threshold. Enforced for compliance with supplier MAP agreements and FTC advertising standards.
reference: FTC Advertising Standards — MAP Policy; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Floor

description: The initial retail price at which the SKU was first offered for sale in this zone and channel, prior to any markdowns or price changes. Used for markdown optimization and sell-through rate analysis.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Original Retail; FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: The maximum allowable retail price for this SKU in this zone and channel. Prevents price gouging and ensures compliance with consumer protection regulations. Used in dynamic pricing guardrails.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Ceiling; FTC Consumer Protection; CPSC Pricing Guidelines

description: Business reason code or description explaining why this price was set or changed. Examples: 'Competitive match', 'Seasonal markdown', 'Clearance', 'Cost increase', 'Promotional event'. Supports price change audit trail and markdown optimization analysis.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Change Reason; FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: The minimum allowable retail price for this SKU in this zone and channel, below which the price cannot be set without executive override. Protects gross margin and prevents below-cost selling. Distinct from MAP which is a supplier-imposed advertising constraint.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Floor; FASB ASC 330 Inventory Valuation

description: The normalized price per standard unit (e.g., price per 100g, price per litre) used for shelf-edge price comparison display. Required by consumer protection regulations for grocery and FMCG categories to enable fair price comparison.
reference: FTC Unit Pricing Regulations; FDA Food Labeling Requirements; NRF Shelf Pricing Standards

business_glossary_term: Price Per Unit Unit of Measure
description: The unit of measure denominator for the price_per_unit_display field (e.g., '100G', '1L', '1OZ'). Required alongside price_per_unit_display for regulatory shelf-edge unit pricing compliance.
reference: FTC Unit Pricing Regulations; FDA Food Labeling Requirements

description: Numeric priority rank used by the price resolution engine to determine which price list takes precedence when multiple price lists apply to the same SKU-zone-channel combination. Lower integer = higher priority. Drives POS and digital channel price resolution logic.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price List Priority; SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR) — Price Resolution

description: Classification of the pricing strategy applied to this SKU-price-list-zone-channel binding. Supports EDLP (Everyday Low Price), Hi-Lo (High-Low Pricing Strategy), clearance, competitive match, markdown, and promotional pricing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: edlp|hi_lo|clearance|competitive_match|markdown|promotional — promote to reference product]
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Event Type; NRF Pricing Standards

description: The current regular retail selling price for the SKU in this price list, zone, and channel context. Represents the Average Unit Retail (AUR) — the price a customer pays before any promotional discount or markdown is applied.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Retail Price; FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this price record originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer. Values: RPM = the retail merchandising system Price Management, SAP = SAP S/4HANA, ORMS = the retail merchandising system Merchandising System, SFCC = the e-commerce platform, CAR = SAP Customer Activity Repository.
reference: Informatica MDM — Source System Lineage; ISO 27001 Data Governance

description: The native price record identifier from the originating operational system (e.g., the retail merchandising system ID, SAP condition record number). Enables bi-directional traceability between the Silver Layer and the system of record for audit and reconciliation.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) — Price Event ID; SAP S/4HANA SD — Condition Record; Informatica MDM

description: Tax classification code applied to this SKU for VAT, GST, or sales tax calculation at Point of Sale (POS). Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI/CO tax configuration. Determines the applicable tax rate for price display and checkout.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Tax Code; FDA Food Labeling (tax-exempt grocery items); FASB ASC 606

description: The unit of measure for which the retail_price applies (e.g., EA = Each, KG = Kilogram, LB = Pound, L = Litre). Critical for price-per-unit display compliance and weight-based pricing at POS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|KG|LB|L|ML|M|FT|OZ|PK|CS — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: GS1 Unit of Measure Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) — UOM; FDA Food Labeling Requirements

description: The date and time at which this SKU price record was last modified in the Silver Layer data product. Tracks price change events and supports audit trail requirements for pricing governance.
reference: ISO 27001 Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity; FASB SOX Compliance

description: Unique surrogate identifier for this assignment record. Primary key enabling tracking of individual price list deployments to zones.

business_glossary_term: Zone Price List Assignment - Price List Id
description: Foreign key linking to the price list being assigned to the zone. References the pricing strategy container that defines SKU-level prices.

business_glossary_term: Zone Price List Assignment - Price Zone Id
description: Foreign key linking to the price zone receiving the price list assignment. References the geographic or market segment where the pricing strategy will be applied.

Workflow approval state of this assignment within pricing governance processes. DRAFT = under construction; PENDING_APPROVAL = submitted for review; APPROVED = active or scheduled; REJECTED = denied by pricing authority; EXPIRED = past effective end date.
Name or employee identifier of the pricing director or regional manager who approved this assignment. Required for assignments that cross approval thresholds.
Date and time when this assignment was formally approved. Used in compliance reporting and pricing change audit trails.
Name or employee identifier of the pricing analyst or merchandising manager who created this assignment. Supports accountability and workflow tracking.
Date and time when this assignment record was created in the retail merchandising system audit trail and pricing change history analysis.
Business reason for this specific price list assignment. Examples: NEW_MARKET_ENTRY, COMPETITIVE_RESPONSE, SEASONAL_STRATEGY, CLEARANCE_EVENT. Supports audit and pricing strategy analysis.

Exchange rate applied when the price list currency differs from the zone currency. Enables cross-border pricing strategies with zone-specific conversion rates that may differ from corporate treasury rates.
The calendar date after which this price list ceases to govern pricing within the assigned zone. Supports planned pricing strategy transitions and promotional windows.
The calendar date from which this price list becomes active for price resolution within the assigned zone. Enables time-based pricing strategy rollouts.
The assignment identifier as it exists in the originating source system. Enables traceability and reconciliation with the retail merchandising system or SAP Retail.
Indicates whether this assignment is currently active and participating in price resolution. Allows temporary suspension without deleting the assignment record.

JSON or structured text defining zone-specific pricing rules that modify the base price list behavior. Examples include competitive match rules, minimum margin floors, or promotional restrictions unique to this zone-list combination.
Numeric rank determining precedence when multiple price lists are simultaneously active for the same zone. Lower numbers indicate higher priority in price resolution logic.
Code identifying the operational system of record from which this assignment originated (e.g., RPM, SAP_RETAIL, CUSTOM_PRICING_ENGINE).
Unique surrogate identifier for each competitive price observation record in the pricing domain. Primary key for the competitive_price data product.
Identifier for the specific competitor store location or online channel URL where the price was observed. Enables store-level competitive analysis and geographic price gap tracking.

Foreign key linking to pricing.price_strategy. Business justification: Competitive price observations inform pricing strategy decisions. Adding price_strategy_id FK links observations to the strategy they inform. Removes pricing_strategy_type STRING as redundant.

Reference to the price zone in which the competitive observation was made. Price zones define geographic or market segments used in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) for zone-based pricing governance.

Foreign key linking to compliance.privacy_assessment. Business justification: Competitive price intelligence systems collecting/processing customer data (loyalty card prices, personalized offers) require privacy assessments under GDPR/CCPA. Assessments govern data collection/us

Foreign key linking to promotion.promo_campaign. Business justification: Competitive price monitoring triggers promotional responses. Retailers must track which campaigns were launched in response to competitor pricing moves for competitive intelligence, promotional ROI an
Reference to the internal SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) for which the competitive price observation was captured. Links the observation to the retailer's own product master.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification

description: Foreign key linking to pricing.sku_price. Business justification: Competitive price observations compare competitor prices against our own retail price. Adding sku_price_id FK links to authoritative retail price record. Removes own_retail_price DECIMAL as redundant
add column supplier_vendor_id (BIGINT) with FK to supplier.vendor.vendor_id - competitive prices from marketplace sellers need vendor identification for price matching strategies

Merchandise category code for the observed SKU, aligned with the retailer's category management hierarchy. Enables category-level competitive index aggregation and assortment breadth analysis across competitive observations.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification

description: Sales channel through which the competitor price was observed. Distinguishes between in-store shelf prices, e-commerce website prices, mobile app prices, and third-party marketplace listings to support omnichannel competitive analysis.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Indicates whether the competitor had the product in stock at the time of the price observation (True = in stock, False = out of stock). Out-of-stock competitor observations may reduce the urgency of a price response.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Name of the competing retailer or marketplace whose price was observed (e.g., Walmart, Target, Amazon). Used for competitive index tracking and Hi-Lo / EDLP strategy calibration.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Numeric pack size or quantity of the competitor's product offering (e.g., 12 for a 12-pack, 1.5 for 1.5 liters). Combined with competitor_unit_of_measure to normalize prices to a common unit for accurate like-for-like competitive comparisons.
reference: GS1 Global Product Classification; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: The retail selling price observed at the competitor for the matched product, expressed in the local currency. This is the primary competitive intelligence data point used for price gap analysis, competitive index calculation, and pricing response recommendations.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

description: Product name or description as listed by the competitor for the observed item. Used for like-for-like and comparable match validation, especially when GTIN-based exact matching is not available.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); GS1 Global Product Classification

description: Date on which the competitor's promotional price is expected to expire, if known. Enables time-sensitive pricing response planning and markdown optimization scheduling.

Indicates whether the observed competitor price is a promotional or temporary price (True) rather than the regular everyday price (False). Critical for distinguishing Hi-Lo promotional pricing from EDLP baseline prices in competitive analysis.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

description: Type of promotional pricing mechanism observed at the competitor when competitor_promo_flag is True. Includes Temporary Price Reduction (TPR), clearance markdown, loyalty card price, bundle deal, coupon redemption, or rollback. Supports Hi-Lo strategy calibration and promotional response planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tpr|clearance|loyalty_price|bundle|coupon|rollback — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: The competitor's own SKU or item code for the observed product. Supports cross-reference mapping between own assortment and competitor assortment for comparable product matching.
reference: GS1 Global Product Classification; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Unit of measure for the competitor's observed price (e.g., each, lb, kg, liter). Required for unit-price normalization when comparing products sold in different pack sizes or weights to ensure valid price-per-unit competitive comparisons. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: each|lb|kg|oz|liter|ml|pack|case — promote to reference product if additional UOMs are needed]
reference: GS1 Global Product Classification; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Web URL of the competitor's product listing page where the price was observed for online channel observations. Provides a direct audit trail link to the source of the competitive price data for web scrape and third-party feed validations.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Advertising Standards

description: Timestamp when this competitive price observation record was first created in the Silver Layer data product. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and GDPR/CCPA data retention compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability); CCPA; ISO 27001 Information Security

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the competitor observed price (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Required for multi-currency competitive analysis in cross-border retail operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FASB ASC 830 Foreign Currency Matters

description: Method by which the competitor price was collected. Distinguishes between manual in-store surveys, automated third-party competitive intelligence feeds, web scraping, EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) feeds, and mystery shopping programs. Affects confidence scoring and data quality weighting.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); GS1 EDI Standards; FTC Advertising Standards

description: Name of the third-party competitive intelligence provider or data feed vendor supplying the price observation (e.g., Profitero, Nielsen, Numerator, Wiser). Null for internally collected observations (manual survey, mystery shop).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Merchandise department code for the observed SKU within the retailer's organizational hierarchy. Supports department-level competitive pricing governance and GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) impact analysis.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); SAP S/4HANA Retail MM Module

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country/market code where the competitive observation was made. Supports multi-market competitive intelligence aggregation and cross-border pricing strategy governance.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Country Codes; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: GS1-standard Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) used to uniquely identify the product observed at the competitor. Enables high-confidence exact-match comparisons across retailers using a universal product identifier. Includes UPC-A (12-digit), EAN-13 (13-digit), and GTIN-14 formats.
reference: GS1 GTIN Standard; CPSC Product Identification Requirements

description: Numeric score (0.00–100.00) representing the confidence level that the competitor product is a true comparable match to the retailer's own SKU. Derived from GTIN exact match, product attribute similarity, or algorithmic matching. Higher scores indicate stronger comparability for pricing decisions.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Informatica MDM

description: Classification of how the competitor product was matched to the retailer's own SKU. Exact GTIN/UPC matches carry the highest confidence; like-for-like and comparable matches involve attribute-based similarity; private label equivalent matches compare store brand to national brand. Drives weighting in competitive index calculations.
reference: GS1 GTIN Standard; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Competitor price normalized to a standard unit of measure (e.g., price per kg, price per liter) to enable valid cross-pack-size competitive comparisons. Computed from competitor_price, competitor_pack_size, and competitor_unit_of_measure. Essential for grocery and FMCG category competitive analysis.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FDA Food Labeling Requirements

description: Calendar date on which the competitor price was observed or collected. The principal business event date for this record. Used for time-series competitive trend analysis and markdown optimization timing.

Data quality assessment status for the competitive price observation. Verified observations have been validated against a secondary source; unverified are raw inputs; suspect observations have anomalies flagged for review; rejected observations are excluded from competitive index calculations.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Precise date and time at which the competitor price was captured, including timezone offset. Provides intraday granularity for dynamic pricing use cases and web-scrape frequency analysis. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

The competitor's price from the immediately preceding observation for the same SKU and competitor. Enables point-in-time price change detection and price gap trend calculation without requiring a self-join on historical records.
Date of the immediately preceding competitive price observation for the same SKU and competitor. Used alongside previous_competitor_price to compute price gap trend direction and velocity.

Absolute monetary difference between the retailer's own retail price and the competitor's observed price (own_retail_price minus competitor_price). A positive value indicates the retailer is priced higher; negative indicates the retailer is priced lower. Core metric for competitive index tracking and price war early warning.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Price gap expressed as a percentage of the retailer's own retail price ((own_retail_price - competitor_price) / own_retail_price * 100). Enables normalized cross-category competitive index tracking and Hi-Lo / EDLP strategy calibration independent of absolute price levels.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Directional trend of the price gap compared to the previous observation for the same SKU and competitor. Indicates whether the competitive position is improving (narrowing), deteriorating (widening), stable, or has reversed polarity. Supports price war early warning detection.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Ratio of the retailer's own retail price to the competitor's observed price (own_retail_price / competitor_price). A value above 1.0 indicates the retailer is priced higher than the competitor; below 1.0 indicates a price advantage. Core KPI for competitive pricing governance and EDLP positioning.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: System-recommended or analyst-assigned pricing response action based on the competitive observation. Options include: match competitor price, undercut competitor price, hold current price, continue monitoring, or escalate to pricing manager. Feeds competitive pricing rules in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Date on which the recommended pricing response action was implemented in the retailer's own pricing system. Used for measuring response latency and audit trail completeness.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: Current workflow status of the recommended pricing response action. Tracks whether the response has been reviewed, approved, rejected, implemented in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM), or has expired without action. Supports price change audit trail requirements.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: Timestamp when this competitive price observation record was last modified, such as when the response_status was updated or observation_quality_flag was revised. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability); CCPA; ISO 27001 Information Security

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each margin target record in the pricing domain. Primary key for the margin_target data product.
Reference to the merchandise buyer responsible for the category or department covered by this margin target. Enables accountability tracking and buyer-level margin performance reporting.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Workday HCM

description: Reference to the product subcategory within the category (e.g., Jackets within Men's Outerwear) for which this margin target is set. Enables granular margin guardrail enforcement at the subcategory level.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Merchandise Hierarchy Standards

description: Reference to the merchandise department (e.g., Grocery, Apparel, Electronics) to which this margin target applies. Aligns with the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS) department hierarchy.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Merchandise Hierarchy Standards

description: Reference to the product category within the department (e.g., Men's Outerwear, Fresh Produce, Laptops) for which this margin target is defined. Supports category management and assortment planning.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Category Management Standards

description: Foreign key linking to pricing.price_strategy. Business justification: Margin targets are set according to pricing strategy (e.g., Hi-Lo strategy has different margin targets than EDLP). Links margin planning to strategy.

Reference to the price zone for which this margin target applies. Price zones group stores or regions with similar competitive pricing environments. Enables zone-level margin governance in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards

description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Margin targets are set at profit center level for financial planning and performance tracking. Core retail process: profit center margin planning, budget setting, and actual-to-target variance analysi

Foreign key linking to promotion.promo_campaign. Business justification: Promotional campaigns must respect departmental margin targets. Retailers link margin targets to campaigns for pre-campaign margin impact analysis, promotional budget allocation, and post-campaign per

Foreign key linking to compliance.risk_register. Business justification: Margin target risks (inability to achieve targets due to regulatory constraints, competitive pressure, cost inflation) tracked in compliance risk registers. Risk owners monitor target achievement.

Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Margin targets are set by planning season because seasonal merchandise has different cost structures and markdown expectations (Spring/Fall apparel, holiday electronics). Season-specific margin target
The calendar date on which this margin target was formally approved by the authorized merchandise planning or finance leader. Required for audit trail and governance documentation.
Name or employee identifier of the merchandise planning or finance leader who formally approved this margin target. Supports governance, accountability, and audit trail requirements.
reference: Internal Audit Standards; FASB ASC 606; NRF Governance Standards

description: Planned Average Selling Price (ASP) for the category or subcategory during the planning period, in the denominated currency. ASP accounts for all promotional and markdown events and may differ from AUR when mix effects are significant.
reference: NRF Retail KPI Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

description: Planned Average Unit Retail (AUR) price point for the category or subcategory during the planning period, in the denominated currency. AUR is a key retail KPI representing the average selling price per unit and is used to validate margin targets against pricing strategy.
reference: NRF Retail KPI Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Classifies the brand type for which this margin target applies. 'private_label' refers to store-owned brands; 'national_brand' refers to manufacturer brands; 'exclusive_brand' refers to retailer-exclusive third-party brands; 'licensed_brand' refers to licensed intellectual property brands. Supports private label vs. national brand differential margin targeting.
reference: NRF Private Label Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Percentage of the total markdown budget that has been consumed, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.6500 = 65.00%). Calculated as consumed markdown budget divided by total markdown budget. Used to monitor markdown pacing against plan.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Financial Planning Standards

description: The retail channel to which this margin target applies. 'all' means the target spans all channels; 'store' means brick-and-mortar only; 'ecommerce' means digital commerce only; 'bopis' means Buy Online Pick Up In Store (BOPIS); 'wholesale' means B2B wholesale channel.
reference: NRF Omnichannel Standards; Salesforce Commerce Cloud

business_glossary_term: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Rate Percentage
description: Planned Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) as a percentage of net sales for the planning period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.5800 = 58.00%). Complements the gross margin target and is used for cost-plus margin validation in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM).
reference: FASB ASC 330 Inventory; SAP S/4HANA CO Module; NRF Financial Planning Standards

description: The timestamp when this margin target record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting.
reference: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Audit Standards

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all monetary margin target values (markdown budget, etc.) are denominated (e.g., 'USD', 'GBP', 'EUR'). Supports multi-currency retail operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; GS1 Global Standards

description: The calendar date on which this margin target expires and is no longer binding. Nullable for open-ended targets. Marks the close of the planning period for OTB and markdown budget reconciliation.
reference: FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: The calendar date from which this margin target becomes active and binding for pricing governance and markdown budget control. Aligns with the start of the planning period.
reference: FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

business_glossary_term: Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) Target
description: Planned Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) threshold for the planning period, expressed as a ratio (e.g., 2.5000 = $2.50 gross margin per $1.00 of average inventory investment). Used to evaluate inventory productivity and pricing efficiency.
reference: NRF GMROI Standards; FASB ASC 330 Inventory; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Indicates whether this margin target record is locked and cannot be further revised. When True, the target is frozen for the planning period and no additional budget revisions are permitted. Used to enforce financial close controls.
reference: Internal Audit Standards; FASB ASC 606; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this margin target record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance.
reference: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Audit Standards

description: Actual markdown dollars consumed against the total markdown budget as of the last refresh. Tracks cumulative markdown spend to date within the planning period, enabling real-time budget utilization monitoring.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP S/4HANA CO Module; FASB ASC 606

description: Remaining markdown budget available for the planning period, calculated as total markdown budget minus consumed markdown budget. Provides planners with real-time visibility into available markdown capacity.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF OTB Planning Standards

description: Total planned markdown budget in currency units allocated for the planning period, equivalent to the Open-to-Buy (OTB) markdown dollars. Represents the maximum allowable markdown spend to achieve sell-through targets without breaching margin floors.
reference: NRF OTB Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606

description: The pricing and markdown strategy governing how markdowns are applied within this margin target. 'edlp' = Everyday Low Price (EDLP); 'hi_lo' = High-Low promotional pricing; 'clearance' = end-of-season clearance markdown; 'dynamic' = algorithmic dynamic pricing; 'cost_plus' = cost-plus margin-based pricing.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards; FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

description: The absolute minimum acceptable gross margin percentage below which pricing decisions must not fall, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.2500 = 25.00%). Acts as a hard pricing guardrail to prevent margin erosion during markdowns or promotional events.
reference: FASB ASC 606; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards

description: Free-text field for category managers or merchandise planners to capture contextual notes, assumptions, or exceptions related to this margin target, such as competitive market conditions, supplier cost changes, or seasonal demand anomalies.
reference: NRF Merchandise Planning Standards; Internal Data Governance Standards

description: Business label identifying the specific planning period, such as 'Spring 2025', 'Q3 FY2025', 'October 2025', or 'FY2025'. Used for display and reporting in merchandise planning and financial P&L reviews.
reference: NRF Retail Financial Planning Standards; SAP S/4HANA CO Module

description: Granularity of the planning horizon for this margin target. Determines whether the target applies to a retail season (e.g., Spring/Summer), fiscal quarter, calendar month, week, or full fiscal year. Aligns with Open-to-Buy (OTB) planning cycles.
reference: NRF Retail Financial Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: The incremental gross margin percentage premium targeted for private label (store brand) products over national brand equivalents, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0800 = 8.00% premium). Supports private label vs. national brand differential margin strategy.
reference: NRF Private Label Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Sequential revision counter tracking how many times this margin target record has been revised or updated. Revision 0 represents the original plan; each subsequent revision increments by 1. Supports budget revision history and audit trail requirements.
reference: FASB ASC 606; Internal Audit Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Free-text description of the business reason for the most recent revision to this margin target, such as 'Competitive price response', 'Seasonal demand shift', or 'Inventory clearance event'. Supports audit trail and governance documentation.
reference: Internal Audit Standards; FASB ASC 606; FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this margin target originated. 'RPM' = the retail merchandising system Price Management; 'ORMS' = the retail merchandising system Merchandising System; 'SAP' = SAP S/4HANA; 'MANUAL' = manually entered by a planner.
reference: Informatica MDM; Internal Data Governance Standards

description: The native identifier of this margin target record in the originating operational system (e.g., the retail merchandising system plan ID, SAP cost center plan number). Enables cross-system traceability and reconciliation.
reference: Informatica MDM; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP S/4HANA

description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the margin target record, used in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) and SAP S/4HANA for cross-system reference and audit trail linkage.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); GS1 Data Standards

description: Planned gross margin percentage for the defined scope and planning period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.4200 = 42.00%). Calculated as (Net Sales - COGS) / Net Sales. Serves as the primary pricing guardrail for category managers and merchandise planners.
reference: FASB ASC 606; NRF Financial Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Human-readable descriptive name for the margin target plan, such as 'Q2 FY2025 Electronics Gross Margin Target' or 'Holiday Season Apparel Markdown Budget'. Used by category managers and merchandise planners for identification.

Planned sell-through rate (percentage of inventory sold) for the planning period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8500 = 85.00%). Used in conjunction with markdown budget to optimize markdown timing and depth to achieve margin targets.
reference: NRF Inventory Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Current lifecycle state of the margin target record. 'draft' indicates under construction; 'active' means currently governing pricing decisions; 'approved' means signed off by finance/merchandising leadership; 'superseded' means replaced by a revised target; 'closed' means the planning period has ended; 'cancelled' means the target was voided.
reference: NRF Retail Merchandise Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Planned Weeks of Supply (WOS) — the number of weeks of inventory coverage targeted at the end of the planning period. Used alongside margin targets to balance inventory investment and markdown risk.
reference: NRF Inventory Planning Standards; Blue Yonder Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: Unique surrogate identifier for a pricing strategy configuration record. Primary key for the price_strategy data product in the the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) silver layer.

Foreign key linking to merchandising.buyer. Business justification: Buyers own pricing strategies for their categories. Strategy definition (EDLP vs. Hi-Lo, premium positioning, competitive matching) is a buyer responsibility aligned with category role and assortment

Reference to the merchandise subcategory to which this pricing strategy applies. Most granular merchandise hierarchy scope for a strategy. Nullable when strategy is scoped at category or department level.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC)

description: Reference to the merchandise department (e.g., Grocery, Apparel, Electronics) to which this pricing strategy is scoped. Aligns with the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS) department hierarchy.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Product Classification

description: Reference to the merchandise category within the department to which this pricing strategy applies. Enables category-level pricing governance per the retail merchandising system hierarchy. Nullable when strategy is scoped at department level only.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC)

description: Reference to the geographic price zone (cluster of stores with homogeneous competitive and cost conditions) to which this strategy applies. Supports zone-based pricing governance in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: Reference to the pricing analyst or category manager who owns and is accountable for this pricing strategy configuration. Supports workflow routing and audit trail in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 27001 Information Security; Workday HCM

description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Price strategies are defined per profit center to align with local market conditions and P&L goals. Business process: profit center-specific pricing strategy execution, financial target alignment, and

Percentage change in price above which manual approval is required, regardless of the price_change_approval_required flag. Price changes below this threshold may be auto-approved. Null if all changes require approval.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Date and time when this pricing strategy was formally approved for activation by the designated pricing authority. Null if not yet approved. Part of the price change audit trail required for pricing governance.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Minimum AUR (Average Unit Retail) price point allowed for any SKU governed by this strategy. Prevents pricing below a defined floor that would erode brand equity or violate supplier MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) agreements.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; GS1

description: Retail channel(s) to which this pricing strategy applies. ALL covers omnichannel; IN_STORE applies to physical POS (Point of Sale) transactions; ECOMMERCE applies to the e-commerce platform digital storefront; BOPIS (Buy Online Pick Up In Store) covers click-and-collect; MARKETPLACE covers third-party platform listings.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Salesforce Commerce Cloud; NRF Omnichannel Standards

description: Target price index relative to the primary competitor set (e.g., 0.980 means 2% below market average). Used for COMPETITIVE_INDEX strategy type. Drives automated price rule generation in the retail merchandising system competitive pricing module.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; NRF Competitive Pricing Standards

description: Comma-delimited list of competitor retailer identifiers or names used as the reference set for competitive index pricing calculations. Defines which competitors are monitored for price intelligence feeds in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: Fixed percentage markup applied over COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) to derive the retail price when strategy_type is COST_PLUS. Null for non-cost-plus strategies. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA CO module standard cost calculations.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; FASB ASC 606

description: Date and time when this pricing strategy record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and pricing governance requirements.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all monetary price parameters of this strategy are denominated (e.g., USD, GBP, CAD). Supports multi-currency retail operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; GS1 Global Standards; FASB ASC 606

description: Indicates whether real-time algorithmic dynamic pricing rules are active for this strategy. When True, prices may be adjusted intraday based on demand signals from SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR) and competitive data feeds.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: Calendar date on which this pricing strategy ceases to govern price rules. Nullable for open-ended strategies. When populated, triggers strategy expiry workflow in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: Calendar date on which this pricing strategy becomes operative and begins governing price rules for the assigned merchandise scope. Aligns with the retail merchandising system strategy activation date.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: Retail fiscal year (e.g., 2025) to which this pricing strategy belongs. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA FI/CO fiscal calendar for financial planning and P&L (Profit and Loss) reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; FASB ASC 606; NRF Retail Fiscal Calendar

business_glossary_term: Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) Target
description: Target GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) ratio for merchandise governed by this strategy. GMROI = Gross Margin / Average Inventory Cost. Used as a KPI guardrail to ensure pricing strategy delivers adequate return on inventory investment.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Financial KPI Standards; FASB

description: For HI_LO strategy type: the average percentage discount depth applied during promotional price events (e.g., 25.00 means 25% off regular price). Governs markdown depth parameters in the retail merchandising system for non-Hi-Lo strategies.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Markdown Optimization Standards

description: For HI_LO strategy type: the number of days between promotional price events (the cadence of the high-to-low price swing cycle). Governs how frequently items cycle between regular and promotional price points. Null for non-Hi-Lo strategies.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Hi-Lo Pricing Best Practices

description: Date and time when this pricing strategy record was most recently updated. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer pipeline and pricing audit trail.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5

business_glossary_term: Minimum Advertised Price (MAP) Enforcement Enabled Flag
description: Indicates whether Minimum Advertised Price (MAP) supplier agreements are enforced as a hard floor within this pricing strategy. When True, the retail merchandising system prevents any price rule from setting a price below the supplier-defined MAP.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; NRF Supplier Compliance Standards

description: Indicates whether automated markdown optimization (via Blue Yonder Demand Planning or the retail merchandising system markdown module) is active for merchandise governed by this strategy. When True, system-generated markdown recommendations are applied automatically.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Blue Yonder Demand Planning; NRF Markdown Optimization Standards

description: Supplementary free-text notes capturing exceptions, special conditions, or historical context for this pricing strategy. Supports pricing governance documentation and audit trail.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Indicates whether price changes generated under this strategy require manual approval by a pricing manager before activation. Supports governance and audit trail requirements in the retail merchandising system workflow.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF Pricing Governance

description: Cadence at which pricing analysts review and potentially update prices governed by this strategy. Drives workflow scheduling in the retail merchandising system and aligns with category management review cycles.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Category Management Standards

description: Free-text narrative describing the business rationale, objectives, and scope of this pricing strategy. Used by pricing analysts and category managers for context and documentation within the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Category Management Standards

description: Current lifecycle state of the pricing strategy. DRAFT indicates the strategy is under configuration; ACTIVE means it is governing live pricing rules; SUSPENDED means temporarily paused; EXPIRED means the effective period has lapsed; ARCHIVED means retired from use.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP S/4HANA SD

description: Configured percentage by which private label (store brand) products are priced below national brand equivalents within this strategy scope (e.g., -15.00 means 15% below national brand AUR). Supports private label vs. national brand pricing differential policy.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Private Label Standards; FTC Advertising Standards

business_glossary_term: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) Strategy ID
description: Native strategy identifier from the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) source system. Enables lineage tracing and reconciliation between the silver layer lakehouse record and the RPM operational system of record.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Informatica MDM

description: Retail season identifier (e.g., SPRING25, FALL24, HOLIDAY24) to which this pricing strategy is aligned. Supports seasonal pricing governance and OTB (Open to Buy) planning integration with the retail merchandising system Merchandising System.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Retail Calendar Standards

description: Target sell-through rate (percentage of inventory sold within a defined period) that this pricing strategy is designed to achieve. Used to calibrate markdown depth and timing in markdown optimization workflows.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Blue Yonder Demand Planning; NRF Inventory KPI Standards

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this pricing strategy record originated. RPM = the retail merchandising system Price Management; SAP_SD = SAP S/4HANA Sales & Distribution; ORMS = the retail merchandising system Merchandising System; MANUAL = manually entered in the lakehouse.
reference: Informatica MDM; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP S/4HANA SD

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this pricing strategy within the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) and SAP S/4HANA SD module. Used for cross-system reference and EDI integration.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); GS1 Global Data Standards

description: Human-readable name describing the pricing strategy (e.g., 'Grocery EDLP FY2025', 'Apparel Hi-Lo Seasonal'). Used in reporting dashboards and pricing governance workflows.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Primary pricing strategy classification applied to the scoped merchandise hierarchy. EDLP (Everyday Low Price) maintains stable low prices; HI_LO (High-Low) cycles between regular and promotional prices; COST_PLUS applies a fixed margin over COGS; COMPETITIVE_INDEX tracks competitor price positions; VALUE_BASED prices to perceived customer value; DYNAMIC adjusts prices algorithmically in real time.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards; FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines

description: Maximum acceptable gross margin percentage for merchandise governed by this strategy. Acts as a pricing ceiling guardrail to prevent consumer price gouging and maintain competitive positioning. Monitored against FTC pricing transparency standards.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; FASB ASC 606

description: Minimum acceptable gross margin percentage (as a percentage of net sales) for merchandise governed by this strategy. Acts as a pricing floor guardrail. Used in GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) monitoring and markdown optimization.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606; NRF Financial KPI Standards

description: Unique system-generated identifier for each pricing rule record. Serves as the primary key for the pricing_rule data product within the the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) integrated lakehouse silver layer.

Foreign key linking to merchandising.buyer. Business justification: Pricing rules are assigned to buyers who have approval authority and execution responsibility for pricing actions within their category portfolios. Buyers manage rule activation, compliance monitoring

Reference to the merchandise category (e.g., Fresh Produce, Men's Denim, Laptops) to which this pricing rule is scoped when sku_scope = 'category'. Supports category management and assortment-level pricing governance in the retail merchandising system if rule applies at a different scope level.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Pricing rules enforcing regulatory requirements (minimum markup, unit pricing display, MAP enforcement) are part of compliance programs. Rules implement program controls.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Pricing rules are owned by merchandising cost centers for strategy execution and budget accountability. Business process: departmental pricing strategy ownership, rule maintenance responsibility, and

Reference to the merchandise department (e.g., Grocery, Apparel, Electronics) to which this pricing rule is scoped when sku_scope = 'department'. Aligns with the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS) department hierarchy. Null if rule applies at a different scope level.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification

description: Foreign key linking to loyalty.tier. Business justification: Pricing rules frequently target specific loyalty tiers (e.g., 'Platinum: 20% off electronics', 'Gold: 10% off apparel'). Replaces denormalized text-based tier references with proper FK for tier-based

Foreign key linking to pricing.price_strategy. Business justification: Pricing rules implement the pricing strategy defined at category/department level. Adding price_strategy_id FK links rule to strategy. Removes pricing_strategy STRING column as redundant with price_st

Reference to the geographic or market-based price zone to which this rule applies. Price zones allow differentiated pricing across store clusters, regions, or markets. Null if the rule applies uniformly across all zones. Managed in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) zone configuration.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Zone Standards

description: Specifies the mathematical method used to compute the price adjustment. 'percentage' = apply a % change to the base price (e.g., 15% markdown); 'absolute' = apply a fixed monetary amount change (e.g., reduce by $5.00); 'index_based' = adjust relative to a reference index (e.g., competitor price index, CPI).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: The numeric magnitude of the price adjustment as defined by the adjustment_method. For 'percentage', this is the rate (e.g., 15.00 = 15%); for 'absolute', this is the currency amount (e.g., 5.0000 = $5.00); for 'index_based', this is the index multiplier. Negative values represent price reductions (markdowns); positive values represent increases.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606

description: Version identifier of the dynamic pricing algorithm or rule engine logic applied by this rule. Used for reproducibility, audit, and A/B testing of pricing models. Example: 'v2.1.0', 'v3.0'. Applicable for rule_type = 'dynamic_trigger', 'demand_based', or 'inventory_based'. Null for static manual rules.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 9001 Quality Management; NRF AI Pricing Standards

description: Comma-separated list of days of the week on which this pricing rule is active. Enables day-parting and weekly promotional cadence (e.g., 'MON,TUE,WED,THU,FRI' for weekday rules; 'SAT,SUN' for weekend Hi-Lo swings). Null if the rule applies every day within the effective date range. Format: MON|TUE|WED|THU|FRI|SAT|SUN.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Promotional Calendar Standards

description: The name or employee identifier of the pricing manager or merchant who approved this rule for activation in the retail merchandising system audit trail requirements and SOX internal control documentation. Populated upon rule activation; null for draft rules pending approval.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 27001 Access Control; SOX Internal Controls; FASB ASC 606

description: The date and time when this pricing rule was formally approved for activation by an authorized pricing manager in the retail merchandising system of the price change audit trail required for SOX compliance and FTC pricing transparency. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SOX Internal Controls; FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; ISO 27001

description: The retail sales channel to which this pricing rule applies. Supports omnichannel pricing governance — rules may be scoped to in-store POS (Point of Sale), e-commerce (the e-commerce platform), mobile app, or applied uniformly across all channels.
reference: Salesforce Commerce Cloud; SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); NRF Omnichannel Standards

description: The reference competitor price index value used as the benchmark for competitive match ceiling or competitive pricing rules. A value of 1.0000 = price parity; values below 1.0 indicate undercutting strategy; values above 1.0 indicate premium positioning. Sourced from competitive intelligence feeds integrated with the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; NRF Competitive Pricing Standards

description: The gross margin percentage applied above COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) when the rule_type is 'cost_plus_floor'. Defines the minimum acceptable margin to protect GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) targets. Example: 35.0000 = 35% margin above cost. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA CO (Controlling) module.
reference: SAP S/4HANA (CO Module); Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606; NRF GMROI Standards

description: The date and time when this pricing rule record was first created in the system. Serves as the audit trail creation marker for data lineage, SOX compliance, and the retail merchandising system change management. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SOX Internal Controls; ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all monetary values (min_price, max_price, adjustment_value) for this rule are denominated. Example: 'USD', 'CAD', 'GBP'. Supports multi-currency retail operations across international markets.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; GS1 Global Standards

description: The calendar date on which this pricing rule expires and ceases execution. Null indicates an open-ended rule with no planned expiry (common for EDLP lock rules). the retail merchandising system automatically transitions rule_status to 'expired' when this date is passed. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: The calendar date on which this pricing rule becomes active and eligible for execution. Used by the retail merchandising system's scheduling engine to activate rules at the correct time. Aligns with OTB (Open to Buy) planning cycles and promotional calendar. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

description: Defines how the pricing rule is triggered and applied. 'manual' = merchant-initiated via the retail merchandising system; 'batch' = scheduled overnight or periodic run via SAP S/4HANA SD; 'real_time' = instantaneous algorithmic trigger at POS or checkout; 'near_real_time' = sub-minute latency via the retail analytics platform demand signals.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

description: The date and time when this pricing rule record was most recently modified. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer, and audit trail maintenance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 27001 Information Security; GDPR Article 5; SOX Internal Controls

description: Indicates whether this pricing rule applies exclusively to loyalty program members. True = price adjustment is only available to enrolled loyalty customers (e.g., member-only pricing); False = rule applies to all customers regardless of loyalty status. Integrates with CRM (Customer Relationship Management) loyalty program data.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Salesforce Commerce Cloud; GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis); CCPA

description: The maximum allowable markdown percentage from the AUR (Average Unit Retail) or original retail price for markdown and clearance rules. Prevents excessive margin erosion. Example: 40.0000 = maximum 40% markdown. Used in markdown optimization workflows within the retail merchandising system and Blue Yonder Demand Planning.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Blue Yonder Demand Planning; NRF Markdown Optimization Standards; FASB ASC 606

description: The absolute ceiling price above which this rule must not raise the selling price. Prevents price gouging and ensures compliance with FTC consumer protection standards. Used in competitive match ceiling rules to cap price increases. Expressed in the operating currency (USD). Corresponds to the 'price ceiling' concept in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Consumer Protection Act; FASB ASC 606

description: The absolute floor price below which this rule must not reduce the selling price, regardless of adjustment logic. Protects against below-cost selling and ensures compliance with FTC pricing transparency and predatory pricing regulations. Expressed in the operating currency (USD). Corresponds to the 'price floor' concept in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; FASB ASC 606

description: Indicates whether a manual price override for this rule requires supervisory approval before taking effect. True = approval workflow triggered in the retail merchandising system; False = override can be applied immediately by authorized users. Relevant only when override_permitted = True.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 27001 Information Security; SOX Internal Controls

description: Indicates whether a merchant or store manager is permitted to manually override this pricing rule at the POS (Point of Sale) or in the retail merchandising system = override allowed with appropriate role-based authorization; False = rule is locked and cannot be overridden (common for EDLP lock and regulatory compliance rules).
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Guidelines; ISO 27001 Access Control

description: Integer ranking that determines execution order when multiple pricing rules apply to the same SKU simultaneously. Lower numeric value = higher priority (1 = highest). Used by the retail merchandising system's rule conflict resolution engine to determine which rule wins in overlapping scenarios. Critical for Hi-Lo vs EDLP conflict resolution.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Governance Standards

description: Specifies the price rounding convention applied after the adjustment calculation. 'charm_99' rounds to the nearest X.99 (psychological pricing); 'charm_95' rounds to X.95; 'nearest_cent' rounds to two decimal places; 'nearest_dollar' rounds to whole dollar; 'custom' uses a merchant-defined rounding table in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Best Practices

description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the pricing rule, used in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM) and SAP S/4HANA SD module for cross-system reference and audit trail correlation. Example: 'EDLP-GRC-001', 'HILO-APP-Q4'.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); GS1 Global Data Standards

description: Free-text narrative description of the pricing rule's business purpose, scope, and rationale. Authored by the pricing analyst or category manager in the retail merchandising system context for audit reviews, merchant onboarding, and pricing governance documentation.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Governance Standards

description: Human-readable descriptive name for the pricing rule, used by merchants and pricing analysts to identify the rule in the retail merchandising system dashboards and reporting. Example: 'Grocery EDLP Floor — Q1 2025', 'Electronics Hi-Lo Weekend Swing'.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); National Retail Federation (NRF)

description: Current lifecycle state of the pricing rule within the retail merchandising system whether the rule is eligible for execution in batch or real-time pricing engines. 'draft' = under configuration; 'active' = live and enforced; 'inactive' = disabled but retained; 'suspended' = temporarily halted; 'expired' = past effective end date.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Categorical classification of the pricing rule's business logic. Defines the algorithmic or policy basis for price determination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cost_plus_floor|competitive_match_ceiling|edlp_lock|hilo_swing_limit|rounding|dynamic_trigger|demand_based|inventory_based|time_of_day|markdown — promote to reference product]
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards

description: The target sell-through rate (percentage of inventory sold) that this pricing rule is designed to achieve. Used in inventory-based and markdown rules to drive clearance of dead stock. Example: 85.0000 = target 85% sell-through. Aligns with Blue Yonder Demand Planning replenishment signals and ORMS inventory management.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Blue Yonder Demand Planning; NRF Inventory Management Standards

description: Defines the breadth of SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) applicability for this pricing rule. 'all_skus' applies enterprise-wide; 'category' scopes to a merchandise category; 'department' scopes to a department; 'specific_sku' targets individual SKUs; 'price_zone' applies to a geographic price zone. Aligns with the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS) hierarchy.
reference: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); GS1 Global Product Classification; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

description: The native identifier of this pricing rule in the originating operational system of record (the retail merchandising system Price Management RPM). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the RPM source system for audit and reconciliation purposes.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Informatica MDM; ISO 27001 Data Lineage

description: Indicates whether this pricing rule can be combined (stacked) with other active pricing rules or promotions for the same SKU. True = rule can stack with other discounts/promotions; False = rule is exclusive and prevents other rules from applying simultaneously. Critical for promotion conflict management in the retail merchandising system
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Promotions Management Standards

description: The daily end time (HH:MM in 24-hour format) at which this rule ceases to be active for intraday pricing windows. Paired with time_of_day_start to define the active window. Null if the rule applies all day.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

description: The daily start time (HH:MM in 24-hour format) from which this rule is active, applicable when trigger_type = 'time_based' or rule_type = 'time_of_day'. Enables intraday dynamic pricing (e.g., happy hour markdowns, peak-hour surcharges). Null if the rule applies all day.
reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

description: The numeric threshold value that must be breached to activate the trigger condition. Interpretation depends on trigger_type: for 'inventory_threshold' this is the WOS (Weeks of Supply) or unit count; for 'demand_surge' this is the demand index multiplier; for 'sell_through_rate' this is the percentage. Sourced from Blue Yonder Demand Planning signals.
reference: Blue Yonder Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

description: The business condition or event that activates this pricing rule. Defines what must occur for the rule to fire. reference: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Blue Yonder Demand Planning; SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

Date when this SKU was first authorized to be stocked at this node. Marks the beginning of the assortment assignment. Used for assortment history tracking and performance analysis.
Date when this SKU was removed from the authorized assortment at this node. Null for currently active assignments. Used for assortment history and discontinued product tracking.
Timestamp when this assortment assignment record was created in the system.

Date when this SKU was last received into inventory at this node. Used to identify slow-moving or stale inventory, support FIFO/FEFO rotation, and flag potential obsolescence. Updated by warehouse management system upon receipt confirmation.

Maximum inventory quantity that should be stocked at this node for this SKU. Prevents overstocking and ensures efficient use of storage capacity. Set based on storage constraints, demand forecasts, and inventory turn targets. Node-specific based on storage capacity and sales velocity.

Number of days required to replenish this SKU at this specific node from the time a replenishment order is placed. Includes order processing, picking, packing, transit, and receiving time. Node-specific based on distance from supply source, transportation mode, and receiving capacity.
