Boolean flag indicating whether this image supports zoom functionality on the e-commerce platform. High-resolution images typically enable zoom for detailed product inspection.
Unique identifier for the nutritional information record. Primary key for the item nutritional data product.
Foreign key reference to the SKU product. Links nutritional information to the specific product item.

Foreign key linking to workforce.associate. Business justification: Nutritional labeling requires validation by qualified associates (dietitians, compliance specialists) for FDA compliance, allergen accuracy, and regulatory audit trails. Critical for food safety, liab
Added sugar content per serving measured in grams. Required under updated FDA nutrition facts label rules.
Declaration of major food allergens present in the product. Must identify milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, and soybeans per FALCPA requirements.
reference: FDA Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA)

description: Calcium content per serving measured in milligrams. Required under updated FDA nutrition facts label.
Number of calories derived from fat per serving. Optional field under updated FDA labeling rules.
Total caloric content per serving, measured in kilocalories (kcal). Required on FDA nutrition facts label.
Cholesterol content per serving measured in milligrams. Required FDA nutrition facts component.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains eggs or egg-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains fish or fish-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains milk or milk-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains peanuts or peanut-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains crustacean shellfish or shellfish-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains soybeans or soy-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains tree nuts or tree nut-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains wheat or wheat-derived ingredients. Supports allergen filtering and dietary restriction compliance.
Timestamp when this nutritional information record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Dietary fiber content per serving measured in grams. Required FDA nutrition facts component.
Complete list of ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight as required by FDA labeling regulations. Includes sub-ingredients for compound ingredients.
Iron content per serving measured in milligrams. Required under updated FDA nutrition facts label.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product meets FDA gluten-free labeling standards (less than 20 ppm gluten). Supports dietary restriction filtering.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product is certified halal by a recognized halal certification body. Supports dietary and religious preference filtering.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product is certified kosher by a recognized kosher certification agency. Supports dietary and religious preference filtering.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product is verified as non-GMO by the Non-GMO Project or equivalent verification program. Supports dietary preference filtering.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product is certified organic by USDA or equivalent certifying body. Supports organic product filtering and merchandising.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains no animal-derived ingredients or by-products. Supports dietary preference filtering.
Boolean flag indicating whether the product contains no meat, poultry, or fish ingredients. May contain dairy or eggs. Supports dietary preference filtering.
Timestamp when this nutritional information record was last updated. Supports audit trail and change tracking.
User ID or system identifier of the person or process that last modified this nutritional information record. Supports audit trail and accountability.
Monounsaturated fat content per serving measured in grams. Optional voluntary declaration.
Date when this nutritional information became effective for the product. Supports version control and regulatory compliance tracking.
Date when this nutritional information expires or is superseded by updated data. Null if currently active. Supports version control and compliance tracking.
Source of the nutritional information (laboratory analysis, USDA database, supplier-provided, calculated from ingredients, third-party database). Supports data quality and compliance auditing.
Name of the organization that certified the product as organic (e.g., USDA, CCOF, Oregon Tilth). Null if product is not organic certified.
Polyunsaturated fat content per serving measured in grams. Optional voluntary declaration.
Potassium content per serving measured in milligrams. Required under updated FDA nutrition facts label.
Protein content per serving measured in grams. Required FDA nutrition facts component.
Saturated fat content per serving measured in grams. Required FDA nutrition facts component.

Unit of measure for the serving size (grams, milliliters, ounces, cups, pieces, etc.). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: g|mg|kg|ml|l|oz|fl oz|cup|tbsp|tsp|piece|slice|container — 13 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Numeric value representing the standard serving size for this product as defined by FDA regulations.
Number of servings contained in the package. May be approximate for variable-weight items.
Sodium content per serving measured in milligrams. Required FDA nutrition facts component.
Total carbohydrate content per serving measured in grams. Includes dietary fiber, sugars, and other carbohydrates.
Total fat content per serving measured in grams. Includes saturated, trans, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated fats.
Total sugar content per serving measured in grams. Includes naturally occurring and added sugars.
Trans fat content per serving measured in grams. Must be declared per FDA regulations.
Vitamin D content per serving measured in micrograms. Required under updated FDA nutrition facts label.

business_glossary_term: Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) Registry ID
description: Unique identifier for the GTIN registry record. Primary key for the GTIN registry product.

Foreign key linking to workforce.associate. Business justification: GTIN registry maintenance requires data stewards to ensure GS1 compliance, barcode accuracy, and GDSN synchronization. Essential for master data governance, supply chain integration, and point-of-sale

Foreign key linking to product.sku. Business justification: gtin_registry.sku_code (STRING) should be normalized to a proper FK. GTINs are registered for specific SKUs - this is the authoritative link between global trade item numbers and internal SKU master.

URL reference to the digital barcode image asset (PNG, SVG, or EPS format). Used for printing labels, packaging artwork, and digital commerce applications. Points to asset management system or CDN location.

The barcode encoding standard used to represent this GTIN. EAN (European Article Number bars), UPC (Universal Product Code bars), ITF-14 (Interleaved 2 of 5 for cases), GS1-128 (application identifier barcodes), QR (2D matrix code). Determines scanner compatibility.

The final digit of the GTIN calculated using GS1 check digit algorithm (modulo 10). Used to validate GTIN integrity during scanning and data entry. Automatically calculated but stored for validation purposes.

Number of child GTINs (next lower packaging level) contained within this GTIN. For example, a case GTIN with child_gtin_quantity=24 contains 24 unit GTINs. Null for unit-level GTINs. Used to calculate inventory at different packaging levels.

ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where this GTIN is authorized for sale. A single SKU may have different GTINs for different countries due to regulatory labeling requirements. For example, USA, CAN, MEX, GBR, DEU, FRA.
Timestamp when this GTIN registry record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Immutable after initial creation.

Date when this GTIN is retired and should no longer be used in new transactions. Null for active GTINs. Used for product lifecycle management and to prevent ordering of discontinued items. Historical transactions retain the GTIN for audit purposes.

Date when this GTIN becomes active and can be used in transactions. For new product launches, this is the go-live date. For packaging changes, this is when the new GTIN replaces the old one. Critical for supply chain cutover planning.
Timestamp of the most recent successful synchronization of this GTIN data to the GDSN data pool. Used to track data freshness and identify GTINs requiring re-publication after attribute changes.

business_glossary_term: Global Data Synchronization Network (GDSN) Publication Status
description: Status of this GTIN in the GS1 Global Data Synchronization Network. Published (live in GDSN data pool), unpublished (not yet shared), pending (awaiting data pool validation), synchronized (confirmed by trading partners), rejected (validation errors). Required for supplier collaboration and EDI.
Unit of measure for gross_weight_value. Typically g (gram), kg (kilogram), oz (ounce), or lb (pound). Must be consistent across supply chain for accurate logistics planning.
reference: GS1 Unit of Measure Code List

description: Total weight of the packaged item including product and packaging materials. Used for shipping calculations, freight costing, and warehouse capacity planning. Measured in gross_weight_unit.

The GS1-issued company prefix portion of the GTIN. Identifies the brand owner or manufacturer who registered this GTIN with GS1. Typically 6-12 digits depending on the company size and GS1 member organization.

The actual GTIN barcode value. Can be 8-digit (EAN-8, UPC-E), 12-digit (UPC-A), 13-digit (EAN-13), or 14-digit (GTIN-14/ITF-14) format. This is the scannable barcode number used at POS, warehouse receiving, and throughout the supply chain.

The specific GTIN format type. UPC-A (12-digit North America standard), UPC-E (8-digit compressed UPC), EAN-13 (13-digit international standard), EAN-8 (8-digit short EAN), GTIN-14 (14-digit case/pallet level), ITF-14 (Interleaved 2 of 5 barcode for GTIN-14).

Indicates whether this GTIN is the base unit of measure for inventory tracking. Typically true for the smallest sellable unit (each). All other packaging levels are multiples of the base unit. Used for inventory conversion calculations.

Indicates whether this GTIN represents a consumer-facing unit sold at POS. True for retail each units. False for case/pallet GTINs used only in supply chain. Determines whether GTIN should appear in e-commerce catalog and POS systems.

Indicates whether this GTIN can be ordered directly via EDI purchase orders. True for case and pallet GTINs typically ordered from suppliers. False for unit GTINs that are only sold at retail. Controls EDI transaction validation.

Indicates whether this GTIN represents a variable measure item (e.g., meat, produce, cheese sold by weight). True for items where price varies by weight/quantity. Affects POS scanning behavior and pricing logic.
reference: GS1 General Specifications - Variable Measure Items

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this GTIN registry record. Updated whenever any attribute changes. Used to track data freshness and trigger downstream synchronization processes.
User ID or system account that last modified this GTIN registry record. Used for audit trail and accountability. Links to identity management system for user details.

The unit of measure for net_content_value. Standard units: g (gram), kg (kilogram), mg (milligram), oz (ounce), lb (pound), mL (milliliter), L (liter), gal (gallon), qt (quart), pt (pint), ea (each), ct (count). Must align with regulatory labeling requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: g|kg|mg|oz|lb|mL|L|gal|qt|pt|ea|ct — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: GS1 Unit of Measure Code List

description: The numeric quantity of product contained in this GTIN package. For example, 500 (when unit is mL), 12 (when unit is oz), 1.5 (when unit is kg). Used with net_content_unit to describe package size. Required for GDSN synchronization.
reference: GS1 Global Data Synchronization Network (GDSN) Standard

description: Depth dimension of the package. Used with height and width for cubic volume calculations. Essential for warehouse bin sizing and transportation load planning. Measured in package_dimension_unit.
Unit of measure for package dimensions (height, width, depth). Standard units: mm (millimeter), cm (centimeter), m (meter), in (inch), ft (foot). Must be consistent for all three dimensions.
reference: GS1 Unit of Measure Code List

description: Height dimension of the package. Used with package_width_value and package_depth_value to calculate cubic volume for warehouse slotting, transportation planning, and shelf space allocation. Measured in package_dimension_unit.
Width dimension of the package. Critical for planogram design, shelf allocation, and transportation cube optimization. Measured in package_dimension_unit.

The packaging hierarchy level this GTIN represents. Unit (each/consumer unit), inner pack (multi-pack sold as one), case (shipping carton), pallet (full pallet load), display (retail display shipper). Critical for warehouse receiving and inventory management.

Self-referencing GTIN that represents the next higher packaging level in the hierarchy. For example, a unit GTIN's parent would be the case GTIN. Null for the highest packaging level (typically pallet). Enables resolution of case receipts to constituent unit GTINs.

Current lifecycle status of this GTIN registration. Active (in use), inactive (temporarily disabled), pending (awaiting approval), suspended (compliance issue), retired (permanently discontinued). Controls whether the GTIN can be used in transactions.

Indicates whether this GTIN meets all applicable regulatory requirements for its country of sale. Compliant (approved for sale), non_compliant (blocked), pending_review (under evaluation), exempt (not subject to specific regulations). Enforced by quality assurance and legal teams.

The new GTIN that supersedes this one when discontinued. Used for packaging changes, reformulations, or product transitions. Enables automatic substitution in ordering systems and maintains continuity in assortment planning.
Unique identifier for the item bundle configuration. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to product.sku. Business justification: item_bundle.bundle_sku (STRING) should be normalized to a proper FK. The bundle itself is a SKU in the catalog. This links the bundle definition to its SKU master record. bundle_gtin can be retrieved

Foreign key linking to workforce.associate. Business justification: Merchandising associates create promotional bundles and multi-packs. Tracking creator enables workflow management, approval routing, performance measurement, and audit trails for promotional planning

Foreign key linking to store.store_location. Business justification: Promotional bundles are often authorized only for specific stores or store clusters (e.g., seasonal bundles in tourist locations, regional promotions). Bundle authorization by store is required for pr
Reference to the primary vendor or supplier responsible for providing the bundle or its components. Used for vendor managed inventory and procurement.
The merchandising category or department this bundle belongs to for assortment planning and category management (e.g., Grocery, Apparel, Electronics).
Detailed description of the bundle contents and value proposition for merchandising and marketing purposes.
The customer-facing name of the bundle (e.g., 'Summer BBQ Pack', 'Family Meal Deal', 'Holiday Gift Set').
The selling price of the bundle when pricing_method is bundle_price. Represents the total customer-facing price.

Current lifecycle status of the bundle: active (available for sale), inactive (temporarily unavailable), pending (awaiting approval), discontinued (permanently removed), seasonal (available during specific periods).

Classification of the bundle configuration: fixed_bundle (pre-defined components), mix_and_match (customer selects from options), gift_set (curated gift collection), kit (assembly required), variety_pack (multiple flavors/variants), multi_pack (quantity of same item).
Defines which sales channels can sell this bundle: all_channels, store_only, online_only, bopis_eligible (Buy Online Pick Up In Store), ship_from_store (fulfillment from store inventory).
The quantity of the component SKU included in one unit of the bundle. Supports fractional quantities for weight-based items.
The display order or assembly sequence of this component within the bundle. Used for kit assembly instructions and merchandising display.
The SKU of an individual component item included in this bundle. References the product master catalog.
Indicates whether this component can be substituted with an equivalent item during fulfillment (e.g., out-of-stock scenarios, mix-and-match bundles).
The date and time when this bundle configuration record was first created in the system.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for bundle pricing (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
The fixed dollar discount applied to the component sum when pricing_method is discount_amount.
The percentage discount applied to the component sum when pricing_method is discount_percentage (e.g., 15.00 for 15% off).
The date when this bundle configuration expires or is discontinued. Null indicates no planned end date.
The date when this bundle configuration becomes active and available for sale across all channels.
Defines how inventory is tracked and decremented: component_level (deduct each component SKU), bundle_level (track bundle as single inventory unit), hybrid (track both bundle and components).
The date and time when this bundle configuration record was last updated.
Indicates whether customers can earn loyalty program points on bundle purchases.
The maximum number of bundle units a customer can purchase in a single transaction. Used to prevent stockouts and ensure fair distribution of limited-time offers.
The minimum number of bundle units a customer must purchase in a single transaction. Typically 1, but may be higher for wholesale or bulk bundles.
The user ID or username of the person who last modified this bundle configuration. Used for audit trail and change management.

Defines how the bundle price is calculated: bundle_price (fixed price for entire bundle), component_sum (sum of individual component prices), discount_percentage (percentage off component sum), discount_amount (fixed dollar discount off component sum).
Indicates whether this bundle can be included in additional promotional offers or discounts beyond its configured bundle pricing.
Reference code to the specific return policy applicable to this bundle (e.g., standard 30-day, final sale, exchange only).
Indicates whether the bundle can be returned. Some bundles (e.g., opened gift sets, perishable meal kits) may not be returnable.
Unique identifier for the item cross reference record. Primary key.
The user ID or name of the person who validated this cross reference mapping. Provides accountability for data quality assurance.

Foreign key linking to product.sku. Business justification: item_cross_reference.internal_sku (STRING) should be normalized to a proper FK. This table maps external system identifiers to internal SKUs - the internal_sku is the core link to the authoritative SK
The item_cross_reference_id of the newer mapping that replaces this one when status is superseded. Creates a chain of reference history for audit and troubleshooting.
Identifier of the trading partner (supplier, vendor, distributor, marketplace) associated with this cross reference. Used for EDI transactions and supplier collaboration.
reference: EDI X12 Standards, GS1 GLN Standards

description: Numeric conversion factor used when the external system uses different units of measure than the internal system. For example, if internal system tracks in eaches but external system tracks in cases, this would be the case pack quantity.
The user ID or name of the person or system process that created this cross reference record. Provides accountability and audit trail.
The date and time when this cross reference record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

Current lifecycle status of the cross reference mapping. Active indicates the mapping is currently in use, inactive means it is no longer valid, pending indicates awaiting approval, deprecated means phasing out, and superseded means replaced by a newer mapping.

Classification of the cross reference relationship. Indicates the nature of the external identifier such as supplier part number, legacy item number from a retired system, marketplace ASIN for Amazon or other platforms, vendor-specific SKU, distributor code, or manufacturer code.
The date after which this cross reference mapping is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended mapping that remains active until explicitly terminated.
The date from which this cross reference mapping becomes valid and should be used for system integration and EDI transactions.
The item description as it appears in the external system. Useful for reconciliation and troubleshooting when descriptions differ across systems.
The item identifier used by the external system. This could be a supplier part number, legacy item code, marketplace ASIN, or system-specific SKU.

Specific instance or environment of the external system when multiple instances exist (e.g., SAP Production, SAP QA, ORMS US, ORMS EU). Helps disambiguate cross references when the same system is deployed in multiple regions or environments.

Name of the external or legacy system that uses the external item identifier. Examples include SAP, the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS), Manhattan WMS, supplier EDI systems, e-commerce platforms, or legacy systems. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SAP|ORMS|WMS|EDI|E-COMMERCE|POS|SUPPLIER|MARKETPLACE|LEGACY|OTHER — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The unit of measure used by the external system for this item (e.g., EACH, CASE, PALLET, KG, LB). Used in conjunction with conversion factor for accurate quantity translation.
The unit of measure used internally by the retailer for this item. Provides context for the conversion factor calculation.
Indicates whether this is the primary or preferred cross reference for the given external system. True means this is the authoritative mapping when multiple mappings exist for the same system.
The user ID or name of the person or system process that most recently modified this cross reference record. Provides accountability for changes.
The date and time when this cross reference record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking and audit purposes.
The most recent date this cross reference was used in a transaction or system integration. Helps identify obsolete mappings that can be archived.

A score from 0 to 100 indicating the confidence level in the accuracy of this cross reference mapping. Higher scores indicate greater certainty. Used for automated mappings that may require validation.

Indicates how this cross reference mapping was created. Values include manual entry, EDI transaction, API integration, file import, system migration, supplier catalog load, or MDM system synchronization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MANUAL|EDI|API|FILE_IMPORT|SYSTEM_MIGRATION|SUPPLIER_CATALOG|MDM — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Free-text notes providing additional context about this cross reference mapping. May include special handling instructions, known issues, or historical context.
Name of the trading partner organization associated with this cross reference. Provides human-readable context for the trading partner.

business_glossary_term: Universal Product Code (UPC) / European Article Number (EAN) / Global Trade Item Number (GTIN)
description: The standard barcode identifier (UPC, EAN, or GTIN) associated with this cross reference. Used for point-of-sale scanning and global product identification.
The total number of times this cross reference has been used in transactions or system integrations. Indicates the importance and activity level of the mapping.
The date when this cross reference mapping was last validated for accuracy. Used to track data quality assurance activities.

Indicates whether this cross reference mapping has been validated for accuracy. Validated means confirmed correct, unvalidated means not yet checked, failed means validation found errors, pending review means awaiting manual verification.
Unique identifier for the item hierarchy node. Primary key for the item hierarchy entity. This is the system-generated surrogate key for each node in the merchandise hierarchy tree.
FK to finance.cost_center
FK to finance.gl_account
Foreign key reference to the parent node in the hierarchy tree. Self-referencing relationship enabling tree traversal and roll-up aggregations. Null for top-level division nodes.
FK to finance.profit_center

business_glossary_term: Allows Direct SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) Assignment Flag
description: Boolean flag indicating whether SKUs can be directly assigned to this hierarchy node. Typically True for leaf nodes (subcategory, segment, class) and False for parent nodes (division, department, category). Controls data quality and hierarchy integrity in PIM (Product Information Management) systems.

Target number of distinct subcategories or product families within this category. Assortment breadth measures the range of categories offered. Used in category management and OTB (Open to Buy) planning.

Target number of distinct SKUs (Stock Keeping Units) within a subcategory or product family. Assortment depth measures the variety within a category. Deeper assortments offer more choice but increase inventory complexity and carrying costs.

Name of the category manager responsible for strategic category management, assortment optimization, and category P&L performance. Category managers define assortment breadth and depth targets and drive GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment).

Timestamp when this hierarchy node record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and master data governance. Automatically populated by the customer master data system (Master Data Management) or source system.

Automated data quality score (0-100) calculated by the customer master data system based on completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness rules. Scores below threshold trigger data stewardship workflows. Supports master data governance and continuous improvement.

Date when this hierarchy node is retired or deprecated. Null for currently active nodes. Supports historical reporting and category lifecycle management. Enables analysis of discontinued categories and assortment changes over time.

Date when this hierarchy node becomes active and available for use in assortment planning, purchase orders, and reporting. Supports time-variant hierarchy structures and seasonal category introductions.

External identifier from source system or third-party data provider. Used for cross-system reconciliation, EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) integration, and external reporting. Examples: GS1 category codes, NRF ARTS hierarchy IDs, supplier category codes.

Detailed description of the hierarchy node purpose, scope, and business rules. Includes category definition, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and merchandising guidelines. Used for training, onboarding, and cross-functional alignment.

The level of this node within the merchandise hierarchy tree. Defines the depth and classification granularity. Division is the highest level, followed by department, category, subcategory, segment, and class as the most granular.

Business identifier code for the hierarchy node. This is the externally-known unique code used in the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS) and SAP S/4HANA MM module for category management and reporting. Examples: DEPT01, CAT-ELEC, SUBCAT-TV.
Human-readable name of the hierarchy node. Examples: Electronics, Home Appliances, Televisions, 4K Smart TVs. Used in reporting, planograms, and category management dashboards.

Full path from root to current node using node codes separated by forward slashes. Example: DIVISION01/DEPT05/CAT-ELEC/SUBCAT-TV. Enables efficient hierarchy queries and reporting roll-ups without recursive joins.

Classification of the hierarchy purpose. Operational hierarchies support daily store operations and planograms. Strategic hierarchies support category management and assortment planning. Financial hierarchies align with P&L reporting. Planning hierarchies support OTB (Open to Buy) and MRP (Material Requirements Planning).

Boolean flag indicating whether this node is a leaf node (has no children) in the hierarchy tree. Leaf nodes are the most granular classification level and are directly associated with SKUs. True for leaf nodes, False for parent nodes.

User ID or system account that last modified this hierarchy node record. Supports audit trail, accountability, and master data governance. Captured from the customer master data system workflow or source system authentication.

Timestamp when this hierarchy node record was last updated. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing. Updated automatically on every modification in the customer master data system or source system.

Average supplier delivery lead time in days for this category. Used in demand planning, safety stock calculations, and OTB (Open to Buy) planning. Managed in Blue Yonder Demand Planning and the retail merchandising system Merchandising System (ORMS).

Current lifecycle state of the hierarchy node. Active nodes are in use for assortment planning and reporting. Inactive nodes are temporarily disabled. Pending nodes are awaiting approval. Deprecated nodes are being phased out. Archived nodes are retained for historical reporting only.

Frequency and timing of planned price markdowns for this category. Weekly and biweekly cadences support fast fashion and perishables. Monthly cadences support durable goods. Seasonal cadences align with end-of-season clearance. Event-driven markdowns respond to competitive pressure or excess inventory. Managed in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM).

Minimum order quantity required by suppliers for this category. Impacts purchase order planning, inventory carrying costs, and cash flow management. Negotiated by buyers and enforced in procurement systems.

Boolean flag indicating whether this category is available across all channels (stores, e-commerce, mobile app, BOPIS, ship-from-store). True for omnichannel categories, False for channel-specific categories. Supports unified commerce strategy and cross-channel inventory visibility.

Name of the merchandise planner responsible for demand forecasting, inventory planning, and replenishment for this category. Planners use Blue Yonder Demand Planning to optimize inventory levels and minimize stockouts and overstock.

Pricing strategy classification for this category. EDLP (Everyday Low Price) maintains consistent low prices. Hi-Lo (High-Low Pricing Strategy) uses frequent promotions and markdowns. Premium targets higher-margin positioning. Competitive matches market pricing. Value emphasizes affordability. Managed in the retail merchandising system Price Management (RPM).

Target percentage of category sales from private label (store brand) products. Private label products typically offer higher margins than national brands. Used in assortment planning and supplier negotiations to optimize category profitability.

Inventory replenishment method for this category. Auto uses system-driven replenishment based on demand forecasting. Manual requires planner intervention. Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) delegates replenishment to suppliers. Cross-docking transfers inventory directly from receiving to shipping. Drop ship sends directly from vendor to customer.

Target safety stock level expressed in weeks of supply (WOS). Buffer inventory to protect against demand variability and supply chain disruptions. Calculated based on service level targets and lead time variability in Blue Yonder Demand Planning.

Seasonal demand pattern classification for this category. Non-seasonal categories have consistent year-round demand. Seasonal categories have predictable demand peaks tied to calendar periods. Used in demand forecasting, markdown planning, and inventory optimization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: non_seasonal|spring|summer|fall|winter|holiday|back_to_school — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Numeric sequence for ordering sibling nodes within the same parent. Used for consistent presentation in reports, planograms, and digital storefronts. Lower numbers appear first.

Strategic role of the category in the overall merchandising strategy. Destination categories drive store traffic and differentiation. Routine categories are frequently purchased staples. Convenience categories are impulse or fill-in purchases. Seasonal categories have time-bound demand. Private label vs. national brand classification supports margin optimization.

Target gross margin percentage for this category, expressed as a percentage of net sales. Used in pricing strategy, markdown planning, and category performance evaluation. Supports GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) optimization.
Unique identifier for the item variant relationship record. Primary key.
Identifier of the user or system account that approved this variant or substitution relationship for use. Used for accountability and compliance in merchandising and product data governance.

Reference to the parent or source SKU in the variant or substitution relationship. For variant relationships, this is the parent style or base item. For substitution relationships, this is the original SKU being substituted.

Reference to the child or target SKU in the variant or substitution relationship. For variant relationships, this is the child SKU (specific size, color, flavor). For substitution relationships, this is the replacement SKU.
The date and time when this variant or substitution relationship was approved for activation. Used to track the approval workflow and ensure proper governance of product relationships.

Indicates whether this substitution can be applied automatically by fulfillment systems without manual intervention. True enables automatic substitution during picking when the source item is out of stock. False requires manual approval or customer consent.

Sales and fulfillment channels where this variant or substitution relationship is valid. All indicates the relationship applies across all channels. Specific values restrict the relationship to designated channels. Critical for omnichannel fulfillment and BOPIS (Buy Online Pick Up In Store) and ROPIS (Reserve Online Pick Up In Store) scenarios. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: all|in_store|online|bopis|ropis|mobile_app|call_center — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The date and time when this variant relationship record was first created in the system. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.

Indicates whether explicit customer consent is required before applying this substitution. True means the customer must approve the substitution (e.g., for price upgrades or significant product differences). False means the substitution can be applied automatically (e.g., for equivalent items). Applicable primarily for substitution relationships.
reference: Consumer Protection Standards and Order Management Best Practices

description: Numeric order for displaying variants in e-commerce product pages, mobile apps, and digital catalogs. Lower numbers appear first. Used to control the presentation order of size-color grids and variant selectors.
The date when this variant or substitution relationship expires and is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended relationship. Used to manage product lifecycle transitions and discontinuations.

The date when this variant or substitution relationship becomes active and can be used by merchandising, e-commerce, and fulfillment systems. Supports time-bound relationships for seasonal assortments or promotional periods.

Indicates whether the source and target items can be treated as interchangeable for inventory allocation and fulfillment purposes. True means inventory of either item can fulfill demand for the other. False means they must be tracked separately. Relevant for substitution relationships.
The date and time when this variant relationship record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking and data synchronization across systems.

Free-text field for additional context, business rules, or special handling instructions related to this variant or substitution relationship. Used by merchandising and fulfillment teams for operational guidance.

The price difference between the source and target items. Positive values indicate the target is more expensive (upgrade). Negative values indicate the target is less expensive (downgrade). Zero or null indicates equivalent pricing. Used for substitution cost impact analysis.

Category of food safety hazard addressed by this control point. Biological hazards include pathogens (Salmonella, Listeria, E. coli). Chemical hazards include pesticides, cleaning agents, toxins. Physical hazards include metal, glass, plastic. Allergens are a special category of chemical hazards.
Date when the control point was last validated to ensure it effectively controls the identified hazard. FDA FSMA requires revalidation at least every 3 years or when significant changes occur.
Probability that the hazard will occur if the control point is not properly managed. Combined with severity to determine overall risk level.
User ID or name of the person who last modified this control point record. Supports accountability and change management for food safety plan modifications.
Timestamp when this control point record was last modified. Any change to critical limits, monitoring procedures, or corrective actions must be documented with timestamp for audit trail.

Specific equipment or instruments used to perform monitoring (e.g., Digital probe thermometer Model XYZ, Metal detector Unit 5, pH meter, ATP luminometer). Supports calibration and maintenance tracking.
How often the control point must be monitored and measured (e.g., Continuous, Every batch, Every 2 hours, Daily, Per shift, Each production run).

The procedure or technique used to measure and verify the critical limit (e.g., Calibrated thermometer reading, Metal detector scan, Visual inspection, ATP swab test, pH meter measurement, Time-temperature recording).
Scheduled date for the next required validation of this control point. Used for compliance tracking and audit preparation.
Additional operational notes, special instructions, or contextual information about the control point. May include seasonal variations, equipment-specific considerations, or historical context.

Indicates whether this control point is part of a prerequisite program (basic conditions and activities necessary to maintain a hygienic environment) rather than a process-specific preventive control.
The specific step in the food production or handling process where this control point is applied (e.g., Receiving, Cooking, Cooling, Packaging, Storage, Distribution).
Documentation requirements for this control point including what records must be maintained, format, retention period, and storage location. Supports regulatory compliance and audit trails.
reference: Codex Alimentarius HACCP Principle 7; FDA FSMA 21 CFR 117

description: Specific regulatory citation or standard that mandates or guides this control point (e.g., FDA 21 CFR 117.135, USDA 9 CFR 417, Codex CAC/RCP 1-1969, GFSI requirement).
reference: FDA FSMA; USDA FSIS; Codex Alimentarius

description: Job role or position responsible for monitoring this control point (e.g., Line Supervisor, Quality Technician, Receiving Manager, Sanitation Lead). Used for training and accountability.

Risk severity classification of the hazard controlled by this point. Critical severity indicates potential for serious adverse health consequences or death. Used for risk prioritization and resource allocation.
Indicates whether this control point is part of the supply chain preventive controls program, addressing hazards in incoming raw materials and ingredients through supplier verification.

Scientific or technical approach used to validate that the control point effectively controls the hazard (e.g., Challenge study, Inoculation study, Literature review, Historical data analysis, Predictive modeling).
How often verification activities must be performed (e.g., Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, Before each production run).
Methods used to verify that the control point is working as intended. May include calibration checks, record review, testing, audits, and validation studies.

business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Incident ID
description: Unique identifier for the OSHA-recordable workplace safety incident. Primary key. _canonical_skip_reason: This product is explicitly marked as a duplicate of workforce.osha_incident and should not be generated. However, proceeding with schema design as instructed.

Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: OSHA incidents are tracked under the OSHA workplace safety compliance program. This FK links each incident to the master compliance program record. Cardinality: Many incidents → One program (N:1). Thi

Identifier of the retail location (store, distribution center, or corporate office) where the incident occurred.
Self-referencing FK on osha_incident (related_osha_incident_id)
Unique identifier of the employee involved in the incident. Protected as personally identifiable information.
Reference to a previous related incident if this is a recurrence or follow-up event.
Identifier of the safety professional or manager assigned to investigate the incident.
The specific body part or region injured in the incident: head, neck, back, shoulder, arm, hand, finger, leg, knee, ankle, foot, multiple body parts, etc. Null for non-injury incidents.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1904.12, BLS Occupational Injury and Illness Classification System (OIICS)

description: The date the incident case was officially closed after all corrective actions were completed and verified.
Detailed description of corrective and preventive actions implemented to prevent recurrence: equipment repair, process modification, additional training, policy update, engineering controls, etc.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the estimated cost amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
The date and time when this incident record was first created in the system.
Total number of calendar days the employee was unable to work as a result of the incident, excluding the day of injury. Used for OSHA 300 Log column H.
Total number of calendar days the employee was on restricted work activity or job transfer due to the incident. Used for OSHA 300 Log column I.
Estimated total cost of the incident including medical expenses, lost time, workers compensation, property damage, and administrative costs.
The calendar date on which the workplace safety incident occurred.
Detailed narrative description of how the incident occurred, including the sequence of events, equipment involved, environmental conditions, and any contributing factors.
Business-assigned unique incident tracking number following the format: location code, year, and sequential number (e.g., DC01-2024-000123).
The precise date and time when the workplace safety incident occurred, including time zone information.

Primary classification of the incident: injury (physical harm to employee), illness (occupational disease), near-miss (potential incident with no harm), property damage, environmental event, or vehicle-related incident.

Specific nature of the injury sustained: laceration, strain, sprain, fracture, contusion, burn, chemical exposure, fall, struck by object, caught in equipment, repetitive motion, etc. Null for non-injury incidents.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1904.12, Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Injury Classification

description: The date the incident investigation was completed and findings documented.
The date and time when this incident record was most recently updated.
Specific area within the facility where the incident occurred: sales floor, stockroom, loading dock, parking lot, break room, warehouse aisle, etc.
Name of the medical facility, hospital, or clinic where the employee received treatment, if applicable.
Additional free-form notes, comments, or observations related to the incident that do not fit in other structured fields.

business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) 300 Log Entry Flag
description: Indicates whether the incident was entered on the OSHA 300 Log of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses.

business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) 301 Reportable Flag
description: Indicates whether the incident requires completion of OSHA Form 301 (Injury and Illness Incident Report) or equivalent documentation.
Current status of the incident case in the investigation and resolution workflow.

business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Recordable Flag
description: Indicates whether the incident meets OSHA criteria for recordability on the OSHA 300 Log (requires medical treatment beyond first aid, days away from work, restricted duty, or loss of consciousness).
Indicates whether photographic or video evidence of the incident scene was collected as part of the investigation.
Indicates whether the incident qualifies as a privacy case under OSHA regulations (certain injuries or illnesses where employee name may be withheld from OSHA 300 Log).
Indicates whether this incident is a recurrence of a similar previous incident at the same location or involving similar circumstances.
The date the incident was reported to OSHA or other regulatory authorities, if required.
Indicates whether the incident must be reported to OSHA or other regulatory authorities (e.g., fatality, hospitalization of three or more employees, amputation, loss of eye).
The date the incident was officially reported to management or the safety department.
Identified underlying cause of the incident determined through investigation: unsafe condition, equipment failure, inadequate training, procedural violation, environmental factor, human error, etc.

Classification of the incidents severity based on injury extent, treatment required, and impact: minor (first aid only), moderate (medical treatment), serious (hospitalization), severe (permanent impairment), fatal (death).
Description of the medical treatment provided: first aid, medical treatment by physician, emergency room visit, hospitalization, surgery, physical therapy, etc.
Number of witnesses to the incident who provided statements during the investigation.
The specific work task or activity the employee was performing at the time of the incident: lifting, stocking shelves, operating equipment, customer service, maintenance, etc.
The claim number assigned by the workers compensation insurance carrier for this incident, if a claim was filed.
Unique identifier for the workplace safety inspection record. Primary key.
Employee identifier of the internal safety inspector or auditor who conducted the inspection.

Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Safety inspections are conducted under OSHA and workplace safety compliance programs. This FK links each inspection to the master compliance program record. Cardinality: Many inspections → One program

Foreign key linking to supplychain.dc_facility. Business justification: DC safety inspections are mandatory retail operations covering equipment, hazmat storage, and OSHA compliance. Inspectors need facility-specific context for regulatory reporting and corrective action

Identifier of the retail location, distribution center, or facility where the safety inspection was conducted.
Version identifier of the safety inspection checklist or protocol used during this inspection. Ensures traceability to specific compliance standards.
Calculated compliance score or percentage representing the overall safety compliance level achieved during the inspection (0-100 scale).
Deadline date by which all corrective actions must be completed to achieve compliance.
Indicates whether corrective actions are required to address identified safety violations or deficiencies.
Timestamp when this safety inspection record was first created in the system.
Number of critical or high-severity safety violations identified that pose immediate risk to employee safety or regulatory non-compliance.
Indicates whether emergency preparedness standards were met including evacuation plans, emergency lighting, first aid kits, and emergency contact information.
Indicates whether equipment safety standards were met including machine guarding, lockout/tagout procedures, and powered industrial truck safety.
Indicates whether workplace ergonomics standards were met to prevent musculoskeletal disorders including workstation setup, lifting procedures, and repetitive motion controls.
Indicates whether the location passed fire safety inspection criteria including fire extinguishers, alarms, exits, and sprinkler systems.
Scheduled date for the follow-up inspection to verify corrective action completion.
Indicates whether a follow-up inspection is required to verify that corrective actions have been completed.
Indicates whether hazardous materials and chemical storage met OSHA and EPA standards including proper labeling, SDS availability, and containment.
Date on which the workplace safety inspection was conducted. Primary business event timestamp for this inspection.
Total duration of the inspection in minutes from start to completion.
Free-text notes and observations recorded by the inspector during the safety inspection including specific findings, recommendations, and context.
Business-assigned unique inspection number or reference code for tracking and audit purposes.
Description of the areas, departments, or systems covered by this inspection (e.g., sales floor, warehouse, loading dock, HVAC systems, emergency exits).
Current lifecycle status of the safety inspection: scheduled, in progress, completed, cancelled, or pending review by management.

Classification of the inspection: routine scheduled inspection, triggered by incident or complaint, pre-opening inspection for new facility, regulatory inspection by external authority, incident follow-up, or annual comprehensive audit.
Professional certification or license number of the inspector (e.g., Certified Safety Professional, OSHA 30-Hour certification).
Full name of the inspector who conducted the workplace safety inspection.
Job title or role of the inspector (e.g., Safety Manager, EHS Specialist, Regional Safety Auditor, Third-Party Auditor).
Number of inspection items that did not meet safety standards and failed the inspection.
Number of inspection items that met safety standards and passed the inspection.
Indicates whether the location or facility manager was notified of the inspection results and required corrective actions.
Number of major safety violations identified that require corrective action but do not pose immediate danger.
Number of minor safety violations or observations that represent best-practice improvements but are not regulatory violations.

Overall outcome of the safety inspection: pass (full compliance), pass with observations (compliant but improvements recommended), fail (non-compliant, corrective action required), or conditional pass (compliant pending minor corrections).
Indicates whether external regulatory authorities (OSHA, local fire marshal, etc.) were notified of inspection results or violations.
URL or file path to the detailed safety inspection report document stored in the document management system.
Date on which the formal safety inspection report was generated and distributed to stakeholders.
Originally scheduled date for the inspection. May differ from actual inspection date if rescheduled.
Total number of checklist items, safety points, or equipment units evaluated during the inspection.
Timestamp when this safety inspection record was last modified in the system.

Identifier of the employee or manager responsible for the custody and maintenance of the asset. Used for accountability and asset tracking.
User ID of the person who created the fixed asset record. Audit trail for accountability.
User ID of the person who last modified the fixed asset record. Audit trail for change accountability.

Total cumulative depreciation expense recognized since acquisition. Subtracted from acquisition cost to calculate net book value.

description: Original purchase price or capitalized cost of the fixed asset including installation and setup costs. Basis for depreciation calculation.

description: Date the asset was acquired or placed in service. Marks the start of the depreciation lifecycle.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment

description: Classification code defining the type of fixed asset (e.g., store fixtures, POS terminals, warehouse equipment, vehicles, leasehold improvements). Determines depreciation rules and useful life.

description: Detailed business description of the fixed asset including make, model, and distinguishing characteristics.
Code identifying the physical location of the asset (store number, distribution center code, warehouse ID, or corporate office location).
Externally-known unique asset identifier assigned by the enterprise asset management system. Used for physical tagging and tracking.

Current lifecycle status of the fixed asset. Active assets are in service and depreciating; under construction assets are capitalized but not yet depreciating; retired/disposed assets are no longer in use.
Date the asset was capitalized and added to the fixed asset register. May differ from acquisition date for assets under construction.
Timestamp when the fixed asset record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts (acquisition cost, accumulated depreciation, net book value).
SAP FI-AA depreciation area code distinguishing book depreciation (GAAP) from tax depreciation and other parallel valuations (e.g., 01=book, 15=tax).

description: SAP FI-AA depreciation key code that defines the calculation rule, useful life, and period control for depreciation runs.

description: Accounting method used to calculate periodic depreciation expense. Straight-line is most common for retail fixed assets.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment

description: Cash or fair value received from sale or disposal of the asset. Used to calculate gain or loss on disposal.
Boolean flag indicating whether the asset has been identified for impairment testing under FASB ASC 360. True if impairment indicators are present.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment Impairment

description: Cumulative impairment loss recognized when the carrying value exceeds the recoverable amount. Reduces net book value and is reported in P&L.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment Impairment

description: Depreciation expense amount posted in the most recent depreciation run. Used for monthly P&L reporting and EBITDA add-back calculation.
Date of the most recent periodic depreciation calculation run for this asset. Updated monthly during financial close.
Name of the manufacturer or original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the asset.
Manufacturer model or part number identifying the specific asset configuration or variant.
Timestamp when the fixed asset record was last updated. Audit trail for change tracking.
Current carrying value of the asset calculated as acquisition cost minus accumulated depreciation. Represents the asset's value on the balance sheet.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment

description: Purchase order number under which the asset was procured. Provides audit trail to procurement transaction.
Date the asset was retired from service or disposed. Marks the end of the depreciation lifecycle.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment

description: Estimated residual value of the asset at the end of its useful life. Subtracted from acquisition cost to determine depreciable base.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment

description: Manufacturer serial number or unique equipment identifier for trackable assets such as POS terminals, vehicles, and warehouse equipment.
Expected useful life of the asset in years as determined by asset class and accounting policy. Used to calculate annual depreciation.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment

description: Date on which the manufacturer or vendor warranty coverage expires. Used for maintenance planning and risk assessment.
Unique system-generated identifier for the lease contract record. Primary key for the lease_contract data product in the finance domain Silver layer.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Lease contracts have gl_cost_center (STRING) but no FK to cost_center master. This FK enables cost allocation for lease expenses (ASC 842 compliance).
Reference to the store or facility location covered by this lease. Links to the store master record for operational reporting, comp sales (SSS) analysis, and P&L attribution.
reference: SAP S/4HANA RE-FX; NRF Store Operations

business_glossary_term: Rou Asset Gl Account Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Lease contracts have gl_account_rou_asset (STRING) but no FK to gl_account master. This FK links to the GL account for right-of-use asset under ASC 842. This is the FIRST of two FKs from lease_contrac
Reference to the lessor's master supplier/vendor record in the MDM system (the customer master data system). Enables linkage to supplier payment terms, banking details, and vendor compliance records.
reference: Informatica MDM; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Master

description: Fixed monthly base rent payment amount as stipulated in the lease contract, excluding variable lease components (e.g., percentage rent, CAM charges). Used as the primary input for lease payment schedule generation and ASC 842 liability measurement.
reference: FASB ASC 842-10-15-28; NRF Retail Lease Standards

description: Date on which the lease term begins and the lessee obtains the right to use the underlying asset. This is the measurement date for initial ROU asset and lease liability recognition under ASC 842.

Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the lease contract, used in correspondence with lessors, auditors, and legal teams. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI/CO lease contract object (RE-FX module).
Timestamp when the lease contract record was first created in the system (SAP S/4HANA RE-FX or finance data product). Used for audit trail, data lineage, and financial close process tracking.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts on this lease contract (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Supports multi-currency lease portfolios for international retail operations.
Contractual end date of the non-cancellable lease term. Used to calculate remaining lease term, schedule final payments, and trigger renewal option evaluation workflows.
SAP GL account number for the lease liability recognized on the balance sheet at lease commencement under ASC 842. Tracks the present value of future lease payments for balance sheet disclosure.

The rate of interest implicit in the lease as defined by the lessor, used as the discount rate when readily determinable. Takes precedence over the incremental borrowing rate (IBR) for lease liability measurement under ASC 842. Expressed as a decimal.

The interest rate the lessee would have to pay to borrow funds on a collateralized basis over a similar term and in a similar economic environment, used to discount future lease payments to present value when the implicit rate is not readily determinable. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.045000 = 4.5%). Required for ASC 842 lease liability measurement.

Incremental costs incurred by the lessee directly attributable to negotiating and arranging the lease (e.g., legal fees, broker commissions). Added to the initial ROU asset value at commencement under ASC 842.
Date on which the most recent lease payment was made to the lessor. Used for payment reconciliation, delinquency monitoring, and lease liability roll-forward calculations during monthly close.
reference: FASB ASC 842; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO AP

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the lease contract record, including remeasurements, modifications, and status changes. Supports incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer and audit compliance.

Total lease incentives received from the lessor (e.g., tenant improvement allowances, rent-free periods, moving allowances). Reduces the initial ROU asset value at commencement under ASC 842 and is amortized over the lease term.

Current outstanding lease liability balance as of the last accounting close, reflecting initial recognition less principal payments made to date. Split into current and non-current portions for balance sheet classification per ASC 842.

Present value of future lease payments discounted at the applicable rate (implicit rate or IBR) at lease commencement date. Represents the initial lease liability recognized on the balance sheet under ASC 842.

Current lifecycle state of the lease contract. Drives accounting treatment, payment processing, and disclosure eligibility. 'Modified' indicates a lease modification event requiring remeasurement under ASC 842.

Total non-cancellable lease term expressed in months, including any renewal periods that are reasonably certain to be exercised. Used for amortization schedule generation and ASC 842 disclosure of weighted-average remaining lease term.

ASC 842 classification of the lease as either an operating lease (expense recognized straight-line on P&L) or a finance lease (ROU asset amortized separately from interest expense). Drives balance sheet recognition and disclosure treatment.

Category of the underlying leased asset. Retail-specific categories include store locations (hypermarkets, department stores, discount outlets), distribution centers (DC), dark stores, micro-fulfillment centers (MFC), equipment, and vehicles. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: store_location|distribution_center|office|equipment|vehicle|dark_store|micro_fulfillment_center — promote to reference product]
reference: FASB ASC 842; NRF Retail Property Standards

description: Legal name of the lessor (landlord or equipment owner) as stated in the lease agreement. Used for counterparty identification in AP processing, EDI transactions, and disclosure reporting.

Indicates whether the lease qualifies for the low-value asset practical expedient (typically assets with an underlying value below $5,000 when new). When True, lease payments are recognized as expense on a straight-line basis without balance sheet recognition.
reference: FASB ASC 842-20-25-2; IFRS 16 (reference for international operations)

description: Date on which a lease modification event occurred (e.g., extension of lease term, addition of leased space, change in rent). Triggers remeasurement of the ROU asset and lease liability at the modification date under ASC 842.

Categorizes the nature of the most recent lease modification event. Determines whether the modification is accounted for as a separate new lease or a remeasurement of the existing lease under ASC 842.
Date on which the next scheduled lease payment is due to the lessor. Used for AP cash management, payment run scheduling, and short-term lease liability classification on the balance sheet.
Frequency at which lease payments are due under the contract terms. Drives payment schedule generation, cash flow forecasting, and AP payment run scheduling in SAP S/4HANA.

Indicates whether the lease contract includes an option for the lessee to purchase the underlying asset. A purchase option that is reasonably certain to be exercised is a criterion for finance lease classification under ASC 842.

Indicates whether the lease contract contains one or more renewal options. When True, renewal_option_term_months and renewal_reasonably_certain_flag must be evaluated for inclusion in the lease term under ASC 842.
Duration in months of the renewal option period(s) available under the lease contract. Included in the lease term measurement when the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise the option.

Indicates whether the lessee has determined it is reasonably certain to exercise the renewal option, requiring inclusion of the renewal period in the lease term and remeasurement of ROU asset and lease liability under ASC 842.

Current net book value of the ROU asset after accumulated amortization (finance lease) or straight-line adjustments (operating lease) as of the last accounting close date. Used for balance sheet presentation and ASC 842 disclosure.

Initial carrying amount of the Right-of-Use (ROU) asset recognized at lease commencement, equal to the initial lease liability plus any lease payments made at or before commencement, less any lease incentives received, plus initial direct costs. Expressed in functional currency (USD).

Indicates whether the lease qualifies for the short-term lease practical expedient under ASC 842 (lease term of 12 months or less at commencement). When True, the lessee is not required to recognize an ROU asset or lease liability on the balance sheet.
Actual date on which the lease was terminated early (if applicable). Triggers derecognition of the ROU asset and lease liability and recognition of any gain or loss on termination under ASC 842.

Indicates whether the lease contract contains an early termination option. When True, the termination option must be assessed for reasonable certainty of exercise, which may shorten the lease term used in ASC 842 measurement.

Indicates whether the lease contract includes variable lease payments (e.g., percentage rent based on store sales, CPI-indexed escalations, or CAM charges). Variable payments not dependent on an index or rate are excluded from lease liability measurement but disclosed separately under ASC 842.

Describes the basis on which variable lease payments are calculated. 'sales_percentage' is common in retail (percentage rent tied to store revenue). 'cpi_index' indicates CPI-linked escalation. 'cam_charges' covers common area maintenance. Drives variable payment disclosure under ASC 842.
reference: FASB ASC 842-10-15-35; NRF Retail Lease Standards

description: Weighted average remaining lease term in years as of the reporting date, calculated across the lease portfolio. Required ASC 842 disclosure for both operating and finance leases in the financial statement footnotes.

Current lifecycle state of the revenue recognition event.
